# James Fox: 'I didn't take that much acid'

This article is more than 12 years old

[Simon Hattenstone](https://www.theguardian.com/profile/simonhattenstone)

At the height of his career, he packed in acting to sell telephone-sterilisers for a Christian sect. As James Fox finally gets a part worthy of his talent, he relives the louche years with Simon Hattenstone

![Image 3: Simon Hattenstone](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/uploads/2018/04/30/Simon_Hattenstone,_L.png?width=75&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)

Mon 2 Dec 2013 14.00 EST

Share

[35 35](https://www.theguardian.com/film/2013/dec/02/actor-james-fox#comments)

[Prefer the Guardian on Google](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=theguardian.com)

J ames Fox is telling me how, at the age of 74, he has finally got his confidence back. Not before time. It's half a lifetime since he walked away from acting, at the height of his fame, to become a door-to-door salesman for an obscure Christian movement.

In his new film, A Long Way from Home, he is desperately moving as Joseph, a man who has retired to France with his wife, only to fall for a young woman travelling with her boyfriend. It's his most dominant role since his incendiary Chas in 1970's [Performance](http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cPdwtFDy7fQ), but it couldn't be more different: Chas was a terrifying cockney gangster in a movie about decadence; Joseph is a restrained, depressed presence in a film about quiet disappointment. Fox's eyes are hollowed out as he observes the world passing by from a distance. He might be dapper and superior in manner, but he aches with longing.

When I arrive at the bar of the boutique London hotel, he is waiting for me, every bit as dapper as Joseph – beautiful navy blue suit, wonderful head of silver hair, military straight-back – and every bit as diffident. He sips on a glass of water, speaks quietly in short, fractured sentences, and chews on his upper lip and fingers.

Fox has an amazing story to tell. There's the acting dynasty: his grandmother and mother were actors, his father was a theatrical agent, his brother Edward is an actor, his brother Robert a producer, his children Lawrence, Jack and Lydia all actors. There's life as a child star, making his debut at 11 in [1950's The Miniver Story](http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=In4_XQqMWaM). There's the tremendous success from the early 1960s onwards that resulted in two great films about fractured identity: [The Servant](https://www.theguardian.com/film/2013/mar/25/how-we-made-the-servant) with Dirk Bogarde, and Performance with Mick Jagger. And, of course, there is walking away from it all at the age of 30.

"I haven't played this interesting a part for years," he says. He's right. In the 34 years since his comeback, there have been memorable roles – humanist headmaster Cyril Fielding in [A Passage to India](http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9afpgqUIu7s), Nazi-appeasing Lord Darlington in [The Remains of the Day](http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2Jq7xgVqPYA), haughty former spy Anthony Blunt in [A Question of Attribution](https://www.theguardian.com/film/movie/96711) – but not enough. The trouble is, says Fox, when he returned to acting, he didn't believe he was up to the best roles. "I came back as a different man and obviously as a worse actor. I hadn't been practising it for nine or 10 years. And I probably lost touch with who I was in terms of my craft, my identity –and other people's perception of me."

One popular theory about why he quit is that he took so much mescaline making Performance it left his head mashed. He says this isn't true. "I was the old pro around that set. I was completely straight. I've always been that in my work. I want to be on the script, I want to know where were are, that we've rehearsed this."

But after making Performance, everybody says ... Fox gently finishes the sentence for me: "I had a crackup." He smiles. So did he? "I don't know. I would have said I was going through some kind of crisis." There was so much going on, he says, and you sense even now he doesn't know where to start. Yes, he had certainly taken drugs when off duty – but, he protests, "I didn't take _that_ much acid." His father was ill with cancer, he was breaking up with a girlfriend. And yes, he did find it hard to leave Performance behind.

![Image 4: James Fox and Anita Pallenberg in Performance](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/static/sys-images/Film/Pix/pictures/2013/12/2/1386003594924/James-Fox-and-Anita-Palle-009.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)

'That was a traumatic film to make' … James Fox and Anita Pallenberg in Performance. Photograph: Allstar/Cinetext/Goodtimes

"It was traumatic to make that film. I'm a [Dirk Bogarde](https://www.theguardian.com/news/1999/may/10/guardianobituaries) in that way. He always said he found it very hard to put the clothes back in the trunk." You can understand why. Everything about Performance was shocking: the violence, the sex (as well as an explicit scene with [Anita Pallenberg](https://www.theguardian.com/film/2008/feb/24/1), Fox snogs [Jagger](https://www.theguardian.com/music/mick-jagger)), the cross-dressing and its overall trippiness. Just watching it can get you stoned.

On the surface, Fox couldn't have been a more enviable symbol of swinging London: he drove flash cars, was papped at the hippest clubs, had girlfriends who were almost as famous as him. He went out with Sarah Miles, now as famous for drinking her own urine (for health reasons) as for her acting. I ask Fox if he ever had a glass of her pee. He starts to giggle and suddenly his tired face is transformed: he looks so boyish. "No, I didn't. I mean, come on! She only started that caper afterwards. Could you imagine!"

I don't know if it's the way the conversation's turned, but I tell him I fancy a glass of white wine. "Oh yes, I'll have one, too. Thank you." He's talking more easily about the past – how he might have looked the part, but he never felt it."I didn't have enough chutzpah. People like [Michael Caine](https://www.theguardian.com/film/michael-caine) and [Terry Stamp](https://www.theguardian.com/film/filmblog/2013/feb/22/terence-stamp-five-best-moments) were good-looking, but they used to pull with their greater confidence and chat." Despite everything, he felt lonely and lost. "I saw a lot of things I didn't like about myself. I'd been having a great time, living a somewhat louche life. But now I felt I'd had it too easy. Guilt, I suppose. Relationships weren't very meaningful."

So he walked away. His crisis expressed itself in a number of ways. "After Performance, I went and did this incredibly naff thing at Christmas in Blackpool, playing Doctor in the House on stage. That looks like a bit of a breakdown, doesn't it?"

Then he left a profoundly secular life in London for Leeds, to work for the Navigators, an evangelical Christian ministry. He gave up his Lotus for an Austin Maxi and survived off a stipend from the Navigators and savings from his previous career. People must have been terrified when Chas rolled up at the door selling God. Well, Fox says, strictly speaking he wasn't selling God – he was raising funds. Doing what? "I was a telephone-sterilising service salesman." Sexy, I say. "Really sexy. God that _was_ sexy!" He gets the giggles again and does an impression of Chas selling door-to-door: "Fackin buy this phone-sterilising stuff or I'll do ya." By the time the wine arrives, Fox has morphed from melancholic elderly man to giddy schoolboy.

Did people ask if he used to be James Fox when he knocked? "They did, yes. They said, 'What are you doing here?' But it was in Yorkshire and there weren't many film buffs there." After a few months, he started doing outreach work with students on behalf of the Navigators. His mission? "To encourage people to have a personal relationship with God." I bet he was a diffident evangelist. "Probably. That's the worst thing to be – a diffident evangelist! He he he he!"

You sense it's taken him decades to see the funny side. "It wasn't good casting – what I was doing for those nine years." Fox often uses the word casting to describe decisions he's made: as if somebody took them for him. Did nobody take you aside and ask what you were doing with your life? "No, I just didn't have the support group, that community. You need friends. A friend." He never had that? "I had a friend at school, a good schoolfriend. I had girlfriends." What about your family? "No, my family – they were so tolerant. They didn't speak." Is that tolerance or uptightness as in: best not to mention what's happening to James? "You said it. Yes, that English thing. Yes."

![Image 5: James Fox and Game of Thrones's Natalie Dormer in A Long Way from Home](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/static/sys-images/Film/Pix/pictures/2013/12/2/1386003676942/James-Fox-and-Game-of-Thr-009.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)

James Fox and Game of Thrones's Natalie Dormer in A Long Way from Home

It might well have been a decade-long flip, yet much good came out of it. He met his wife, Mary, had five children, rediscovered his values. At the age of 40, he decided to return to acting. But for many years, he found it hard to reconcile his Christianity with his work. While Christianity is about subsuming ego, acting is about giving it free rein. As a result, he says he became a boring, inhibited actor. Did any director say: "James, we want a bit of the old Chas back?"

"No, I didn't work with people who took that much interest. Probably, they thought I was a bit of a weirdo anyway. They were wary of me." Does he think he was a weirdo? "Looking back, yes, I do see the weirdo they saw." It took him a while to realise he could still be a good man and play sinners: he was offered the Jeremy Irons role in [The French Lieutenant's Woman](http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oFZPSQKjwwc), but turned it down for moral reasons.

After he returned to acting, he suffered depression, again struggling with his identity. When I watched him in A Long Way from Home, I worried that he was so convincing because he was playing himself. Yes, he says, there were times when he's felt like that, but not now. He no longer goes to church, or is involved with the formal side of religion, but he still considers himself a Christian – one who's more at ease with himself than ever before.

He talks about the love of his family, the support of his wife, how his children are his best friends. "They are so brilliant, what they've done for my life. They take the piss out of you, they're natural with you, just great. My family is the most grounding influence."

Is he ready to return to the more risque roles of old? Yes, definitely, he says – he's done enough repressed, dislocated poshos. It's time to play a hard man, a character with a touch of evil. He throws back his shoulders, puffs out his chest and, in perfectly menacing cockney, tells me: "I've still got a bit of Chas in me."

_A Long Way from Home is out on Friday._

James William Fox, born William Fox on May 19, 1939, is a famous English actor. He has starred in many movies and TV shows. His acting career started in the 1960s. He became well-known for films like _The Servant_. He also played important parts in _A Passage to India_ (1984) and _The Remains of the Day_ (1993).

In the 1970s, Fox took a break from acting. He wanted to focus on his personal life and spiritual beliefs. He returned to acting in the early 1980s. Over time, he became known for playing many different kinds of characters. These included upper-class people and more serious roles. He is part of the famous Fox family of actors.

## Early Life and Family

James Fox was born in [London](https://kids.kiddle.co/London "London") on May 19, 1939. He was the second son of Robin Fox, who was a [theatrical agent](https://kids.kiddle.co/Talent_agent "Talent agent"). His mother was Angela Worthington, an actress. His older brother is the actor [Edward Fox](https://kids.kiddle.co/Edward_Fox_(actor) "Edward Fox (actor)"). His younger brother is the film producer Robert Fox. His grandfather on his mother's side was the playwright Frederick Lonsdale. James Fox studied acting at the Central School of Speech and Drama.

## Acting Career Highlights

### Starting Out in Acting

Fox first appeared in a film when he was eleven years old. He played Toby Miniver in _The Miniver Story_ in 1950. In his early roles, both in movies and on TV, he used his birth name, William Fox.

He also appeared in the film _The Loneliness of the Long Distance Runner_ (1962). In 1964, Fox won a BAFTA Award for Most Promising Newcomer to Leading Film Roles. This award was for his role in _The Servant_ (1963). He worked with actors like [Dirk Bogarde](https://kids.kiddle.co/Dirk_Bogarde "Dirk Bogarde") and Sarah Miles in that film.

On June 16, 1965, the movie _Those Magnificent Men in Their Flying Machines_ was released. This British comedy film was about early aviation. Fox was part of a large international cast. Other films he acted in during this time include _King Rat_ (1965), _The Chase_ (1966), _Thoroughly Modern Millie_ (1967), and _Isadora_ (1968).

### Break from Acting and Return

After working on a film in 1968, Fox decided to stop acting for a while. He became an evangelical Christian. He spent time working with an organization called Navigators. He focused on his faith during this period. The only film he appeared in during this time was _No Longer Alone_ (1976). This movie told the story of a woman who found faith.

In 2008, Fox said that his break from acting was "just part of my journey." He explained that he never stopped watching movies or reading about acting. He felt he didn't miss it because he stayed connected to the world of film.

Fox returned to acting in 1981. He appeared on TV in a show called "Country." This was a comedy-drama set during the 1945 UK elections. He then starred in films like _Runners_ (1983) and _A Passage to India_ (1984). He also played [Anthony Blunt](https://kids.kiddle.co/Anthony_Blunt "Anthony Blunt") in a [BBC](https://kids.kiddle.co/BBC "BBC") play called _A Question of Attribution_ (1992). Other roles included Lord Holmes in _Patriot Games_ (1992) and Lord Darlington in _The Remains of the Day_ (1993).

### Later Roles

After his return, James Fox continued to act in many projects. He was in _The Lost World_ (2001) as Professor Leo Summerlee. He also played Colonel Race in _Agatha Christie's Poirot – Death on the Nile_ (2004). In 2005, he appeared in _[Charlie and the Chocolate Factory](https://kids.kiddle.co/Charlie\_and\_the\_Chocolate\_Factory\_(film) "Charlie and the Chocolate Factory (film)")_. He played Mr. Salt, who was Veruca Salt's father.

In 2007, he was a guest star in the TV crime series _Waking the Dead_. He also acted alongside his son Laurence Fox in an episode of _Lewis_. In 2009, he was part of the cast of _Sherlock Holmes_. He played Sir Thomas, a leader of a secret society.

In 2011, he played [King George V](https://kids.kiddle.co/George_V "George V") in the film _W.E._, which was directed by [Madonna](https://kids.kiddle.co/Madonna "Madonna"). In 2013, he had a main role in the movie _A Long Way from Home_.

## Personal Life

James Fox married Mary Elizabeth Piper in September 1973. They had five children together. Their children include actors Laurence and Jack. Mary Elizabeth Piper passed away at their home on April 19, 2020.

His daughter Lydia is married to actor [Richard Ayoade](https://kids.kiddle.co/Richard_Ayoade "Richard Ayoade"). His son Laurence was married to actress [Billie Piper](https://kids.kiddle.co/Billie_Piper "Billie Piper") from 2007 to 2016.

**Akbar Salahuddin Ahmed** (born 15 January 1943) is a [Pakistani-American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakistani_Americans "Pakistani Americans") academic, author, poet, playwright, filmmaker and former diplomat.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-Nader362-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-AhmedForstxiixiii-3) He currently is a professor of International Relations and holds the Ibn Khaldun Chair of Islamic Studies at the [American University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_University "American University"), School of International Service in [Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C.")[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-Nader362-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-AhmedForstxiixiii-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-Watson219-4) Akbar Ahmed served as the Pakistan High Commissioner to the UK and Ireland. He currently is a Global Fellow at the Woodrow Wilson Center.

Immediately prior, he taught at Princeton University and served as a visiting professor at the [Institute for Advanced Study](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Institute_for_Advanced_Study "Institute for Advanced Study") in [Princeton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Princeton,_New_Jersey "Princeton, New Jersey").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-Nader362-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-AhmedForstxiixiii-3)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-Bennett31-5) He also taught at Harvard University and was a visiting scholar at the Department of Anthropology.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-Bennett31-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-AhmedHart331-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-Peabody3-7) Ahmed was the First Chair of Middle East and Islamic Studies at the US Naval Academy, [Annapolis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annapolis "Annapolis"), and a Nonresident Senior Fellow at the [Brookings Institution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brookings_Institution "Brookings Columbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/District_of_Columbia "District of Columbia") Professor of the Year by the [Carnegie Foundation for the Advancement of Teaching](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carnegie_Foundation_for_the_Advancement_of_Teaching "Carnegie Foundation for the Advancement of Teaching") and the [Council for Advancement and Support of Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Waziristan_Agency "South Waziristan Agency") and Commissioner in [Balochistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Balochistan Cambridge").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-Nader362-2)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-Ahmede133-8)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-Bennett31-5) ## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Akbar_Ahmed&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Career")]

### Living Islam

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Akbar_Ahmed&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Living Islam")]

Hugh Purcell, the executive producer of the BBC television series _Living Islam_ (1993), who worked closely with Ahmed on the production, wrote in a 2025 review that Ahmed’s work over the decades reflects a sustained commitment to peace and “co-existence,” calling it “sorely needed.”[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-14) Purcell, a BBC producer with over two decades of experience, has also stated that _Living Islam_, presented by Ahmed, was the production he was “most proud of” in his career.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-15)

### Civil service and academia

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Akbar_Ahmed&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Civil service and academia")]

He studied at Burn Hall School (now [Army Burn Hall College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Army_Burn_Hall_College "Army Burn Hall College")) in [Abbottabad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abbottabad "Abbottabad") from 1954 to 1959. Burn Hall was founded in 1943 by members of [Saint Joseph's Missionary Society of Mill Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Joseph's_Missionary_Society_of_Mill_Hill "Saint Joseph's Missionary Society of Mill Hill") (MHM) in [British India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_India "British India") as a missionary school for boys. It was ceded to [Pakistan Army Education Corps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakistan_Army_Education_Corps "Pakistan Army Education Corps") in 1977 and was renamed Army Burn Hall College.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-:1-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-hazara-17) Ahmed entered the Pakistani civil service in 1966.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-Bennett31-5)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-WignarajaHussain359-12) He graduated from [University of the Punjab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_the_Punjab "University of the Punjab") and [University of Birmingham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Birmingham "University of Birmingham") and later attended Cambridge University doing an [MA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_Arts "Master of Arts").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-Nader362-2)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-Bennett31-5) In 1978, Ahmed graduated with a [PhD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_of_Philosophy "Doctor of Philosophy") in [Anthropology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthropology "Anthropology") at the [School of Oriental and African Studies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/School_of_Oriental_and_African_Studies "School of Oriental and African Studies"), [University of London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_London "University of London").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-Nader362-2)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-Bennett31-5) At certain points in his life Ahmed held important government positions such as Political Agent for the South Waziristan Agency/North West Frontier Province (1978-1980) and in Baluchistan was Commissioner for the three districts (1982-1988) and Commissioner of the Sibi Division (1989).[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-Ahmede133-8)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-Bennett31-5)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-WignarajaHussain359-12) Ahmed was the founder and served as Director of the National Centre for Rural Development in [Islamabad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamabad "Islamabad") and also a Director of the Centre for Social Sciences and Humanities, University Grants Commission in Pakistan.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-Bennett31-5)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-WignarajaHussain359-12)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-AhmedHart331-6) In 1988 Ahmed became the Allama Iqbal Fellow at [Selywn College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Selwyn_College,_Cambridge "Selwyn College, Cambridge"), Cambridge for five years and by 1993 he was appointed as the first Muslim Fellow.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-AhmedForstxiixiii-3)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-Bennett31-5) He also was the first Pakistani to serve on the Council of the [Royal Anthropological Institute of Great Britain and Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Anthropological_Institute_of_Great_Britain_and_Ireland "Royal Anthropological Institute of Great Britain and "Quaid-i-Azam University") in Pakistan.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-Bennett31-5)

Prior to the Brookings quartet of studies, Ahmed's projects included the Jinnah Quartet and Living Islam. The Jinnah Quartet comprised a feature film Jinnah (1998), with Christopher Lee in the title role; a documentary, Mr. Jinnah: The Making of Pakistan (1997); a graphic novel, The Quaid: Jinnah and the Story of Pakistan (1997); and a biographical study, Jinnah, Pakistan and Islamic Identity: The Search for Saladin (1997). Ahmed presented and narrated the six-part BBC TV series Living Islam (1993) and authored the accompanying book of the same name. Later, Ahmed served as Pakistani High Commissioner (ambassador) to the United Kingdom and Ireland from 1999 to 2000.

### Research interests and literary works

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Akbar_Ahmed&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Research interests and literary works")]

Ahmed's research interests focus on [Pashtuns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pashtuns "Pashtuns") and others including tribal groups, Muslim society and development anthropology.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-AhmedHart331-6) He has conducted anthropological fieldwork with Pashtuns in [Afghanistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afghanistan "Afghanistan"), undertaken comparative studies of Islamic social customs in [Morocco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morocco "Morocco"), [Pakistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakistan "Pakistan") and [Saudi Arabia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi_Arabia "Saudi Arabia") and researching global Islam alongside its impacts on contemporary society.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-AhmedForstxiixiii-3)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-Peabody3-7)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-Hendry233-18) Among his works on Pashtuns are: _Millennium and Charisma Among Pathans_ (1976), _Pukhtun Economy and Society_ (1980), and his wide-ranging study _The Thistle and the Drone_ (2013) that focuses on Muslim hill peoples in Pakistan, [Yemen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yemen "Yemen"), [North Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Africa "North Africa") and afar as the [Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippines "Philippines") which examines [US drone operations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_drone_strike "US drone strike") in the Muslim world, its subsequent consequences and reputation of the USA being considered synonymous with the drone.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-Nader362-2)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-Benthall176179-19) Ahmed has criticized some anthropologists for studying "Muslim groups without reference to the Islamic framework".[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-OsellaSoares15-20) Other areas of research interest include Modernity and Muslims along with Islam and the concept of [postmodernism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Postmodernism "Postmodernism") in relation to Muslim societies, cultures, media and the West.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-Bennett3236-21)

Ahmed has co-edited several books with other academics.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-AhmedForstxiixiii-3) He has authored many articles and more than a dozen books that have won awards such as _Discovering Islam_ which became the basis for a six-part BBC TV series called _Living Islam_.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-AhmedForstxiixiii-3)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-Ahmede133-8) Other books are _Postmodernism and Islam: Predicament and Promise_ which was nominated for an Amalfi Award and _Islam Today: A short Introduction to the Muslim world_ was awarded by the [Los Angeles Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Times "Los Angeles Times") as the best non-fiction book of the year.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-AhmedForstxiixiii-3) Ahmed has written a biography of Muhammad Jinnah, Pakistan's first Governor General.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-Farr180-22) and a study _Journey into America: The challenge of Islam_ based on fieldwork with [American Muslims](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Muslims "American Muslims").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-Ahmede133-8) He has also written plays like _Noor_ and _The trial of Dara Shikoh_ which have been published and staged for audiences.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-Ahmede133-8) Ahmed's publications have been translated into other languages such as [Indonesian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indonesian_language "Indonesian language") and [Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_language "Chinese language").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-Ahmede133-8) Functioning between both worlds, through his writing and broadcasting Ahmed has attempted to bridge the Muslim-West world divide and encourage communication between both groups.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-Bennett31-5) He has expressed admiration of English translations of Islamic classics in assisting him to "discover the riches" of "Islamic cultural legacy" and "appreciate critically the beneficial impact of the West".[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-Bennett31-5)

### Interfaith dialogue

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Akbar_Ahmed&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Interfaith dialogue")]

In the aftermath of [9/11](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/September_11_attacks "September 11 attacks"), Ahmed initiated a series of studies that were published by the [Brookings Institution Press](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brookings_Institution_Press "Brookings Institution Press") covering issues regarding relations between Islam and the West.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-Nader362-2) Ahmed has been engaged in a series of public [interfaith dialogues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interfaith_dialogue "Interfaith dialogue") across the US and abroad with Professor Judea Pearl, father of deceased reporter [Daniel Pearl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Pearl "Daniel Pearl") focusing on divisions between Muslims and the West and between Jews and Muslims.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-Watson219-4)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-Henderson20-23) For their efforts, he and Pearl were awarded the first Purpose Prize by the [Interfaith Conference of Metropolitan Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interfaith_Conference_of_Metropolitan_Washington "Interfaith Conference of Metropolitan Washington") at the [National Cathedral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_National_Cathedral "Washington National Cathedral") and Ahmed received the Herschel-King award for Interfaith Activism.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-Ahmede133-8) He has also been appointed as a Trustee of the World Faiths Development Dialogue by the [Archbishop of Canterbury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archbishop_of_Canterbury "Archbishop of Canterbury") and has received the 2002 Free Speech Award from the [Muslim Public Affairs Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muslim_Public_Affairs_Council "Muslim Public Affairs Council") based in Washington DC.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-AhmedForstxiixiii-3) Ahmed has received accusations of being "a Zionist conspirator" and close to the West however he has felt that "dialogue, harmony, communication and debate" are for Islam and the West the key issues of engagement.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akbar_S._Ahmed#cite_note-Bennett31-5)

**James William Fox** (born **William Fox**; 19 May 1939) is an English actor, known for his work in film and television. He is a member of the [Fox family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robin_Fox_family "Robin Fox family") of actors. Fox's career began in the 1960s through leading roles in films such as _[The Servant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Servant\_(1963\_film) "The Servant (1963 film)")_ (1963), _[King Rat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King\_Rat\_(film) "King Rat (film)")_ (1965), _[Those Magnificent Men in Their Flying Machines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Those\_Magnificent\_Men\_in\_Their\_Flying\_Machines "Those Magnificent Men in Their Flying Machines")_ (1965), _[Thoroughly Modern Millie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thoroughly\_Modern\_Millie "Thoroughly Modern Millie")_ (1967), and _[Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Performance\_(film) "Performance (film)")_ (1970).

In the 1970s, Fox took a break from acting to focus on personal and spiritual matters, returning to acting in the early 1980s. Over time, he built a reputation for playing a variety of roles, including upper-class figures and more serious characters, notably in known for his roles in _[A Passage to India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Passage\_to\_India\_(film) "A Passage to India (film)")_ (1984), _[Patriot Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patriot\_Games\_(film) "Patriot Games (film)")_ (1992), _[The Remains of the Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Remains\_of\_the\_Day\_(film) "The Remains of the Day (film)")_ (1993), _[Jinnah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jinnah\_(film) "Jinnah (film)")_ (1998), _[Sherlock Holmes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sherlock\_Holmes\_(2009\_film) "Sherlock Holmes (2009 film)")_ (2009), and _[Effie Gray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Effie\_Gray\_(film) "Effie Gray (film)")_ (2014).

Fox won the [BAFTA Award for Most Promising Newcomer to Leading Film Roles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Most_Promising_Newcomer_to_Leading_Film_Roles "BAFTA Award for Most Promising Newcomer to Leading Film Roles") for his performance in _The Servant_, and was nominated for [Best Actor in a Supporting Role](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Actor_in_a_Supporting_Role "BAFTA Award for Best Actor in a Supporting Role") for _A Passage to India_. He is also a [Golden Globe Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Awards "Golden Globe Awards") nominee.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

William Fox was born on 19 May 1939 in London, the second son of [theatrical agent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theatrical_agent "Theatrical agent")[Robin Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robin_Fox_(theatrical_agent) "Robin Fox (theatrical agent)")[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-1) and actress Angela Worthington. His elder brother is actor [Edward Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Fox_(actor) "Edward Fox (actor)") and his younger brother was film producer [Robert Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Fox_(producer) "Robert Fox (producer)"). Fox's maternal grandfather was playwright [Frederick Lonsdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frederick_Lonsdale "Frederick Lonsdale").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-foxes-2) He applied successfully to study acting at the [Central School of Speech and Drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Central_School_of_Speech_and_Drama "Royal Central School of Speech and Drama").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-cssd-3)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### Early career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Early career")]

Fox first appeared on film as 11-year-old Toby Miniver in _[The Miniver Story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Miniver\_Story "The Miniver Story")_ in 1950.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-acid-4) His early screen appearances, both in film and television, were made under his birth name, William Fox.

Fox appeared in the film _[The Loneliness of the Long Distance Runner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Loneliness\_of\_the\_Long\_Distance\_Runner\_(film) "The Loneliness of the Long Distance Runner (film)")_ (1962).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) His father, [Robin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robin_Fox_(theatrical_agent) "Robin Fox (theatrical agent)"), quarrelled bitterly with [Tony Richardson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Richardson "Tony Richardson") over this, having attempted to forbid his friend from giving his son James (known as "Willie") a part in the film. His father claimed Willie had no talent for acting and should not give up his job in a bank.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-6)

In 1964, Fox won a [BAFTA Award for Most Promising Newcomer to Leading Film Roles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Most_Promising_Newcomer_to_Leading_Film_Roles "BAFTA Award for Most Promising Newcomer to Leading Film Roles") for _[The Servant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Servant\_(1963\_film) "The Servant (1963 film)")_ (1963), working alongside [Dirk Bogarde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirk_Bogarde "Dirk Bogarde"), [Sarah Miles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Miles "Sarah Miles"), and [Wendy Craig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wendy_Craig "Wendy Craig").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-bafta-1964-7) On 16 June 1965, [Ken Annakin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Annakin "Ken Annakin")'s period aviation film _[Those Magnificent Men in Their Flying Machines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Those\_Magnificent\_Men\_in\_Their\_Flying\_Machines "Those Magnificent Men in Their Flying Machines")_ was released. In this British [period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Period_film "Period film")[comedy film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy_film "Comedy film"), Fox is featured among an international [ensemble cast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ensemble_cast "Ensemble cast") including [Stuart Whitman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stuart_Whitman "Stuart Whitman"), Sarah Miles, [Robert Morley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Morley "Robert Morley"), [Terry-Thomas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terry-Thomas "Terry-Thomas"), [Red Skelton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Skelton "Red Skelton"), [Benny Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benny_Hill "Benny Hill"), [Jean-Pierre Cassel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean-Pierre_Cassel "Jean-Pierre Cassel"), [Gert Fröbe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gert_Fr%C3%B6be "Gert Fröbe") and [Alberto Sordi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alberto_Sordi "Alberto Sordi").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-nytimes_066838-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-variety_1200420712-9) Some of the other films he acted in during this time are _[King Rat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King\_Rat\_(film) "King Rat (film)")_ (1965),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5)_[The Chase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Chase\_(1966\_film) "The Chase (1966 film)")_ (1966),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5)_[Thoroughly Modern Millie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thoroughly\_Modern\_Millie "Thoroughly Modern Millie")_ (1967),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5)_[Isadora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isadora\_(film) "Isadora (film)")_ (1968),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) and _[Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Performance\_(film) "Performance (film)")_ (1970).[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-acid-4)

### Spiritual life and break from acting

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Spiritual life and break from acting")]

After finishing work on _[Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Performance\_(film) "Performance (film)")_ (released 1970, but shot in 1968),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) Fox suspended his acting career. The film, which starred Fox and [Mick Jagger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mick_Jagger "Mick Jagger"), was deemed so outrageous that critics at a preview screening walked out, with one film executive's wife reportedly throwing up in the cinema.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-acid-4)

In a 2008 interview, Fox said: "It was just part of my journey...I think my journey was to spend a while away from acting. And I never lost contact with it – watching movies, reading about it ... so I didn't feel I missed it."[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tweed-10)

Fox became an evangelical Christian, working with the [Navigators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Navigators_(organization) "The Navigators (organization)") and devoting himself to the ministry.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-cinema-11) During this time, the only film in which Fox appeared was _No Longer Alone_ (1976), the story of Joan Winmill Brown,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-epit-12) a suicidal woman who was led to faith in [Jesus Christ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesus_Christ "Jesus Christ") by [Ruth Bell Graham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruth_Bell_Graham "Ruth Bell Graham").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-epit-12)

### Return to acting

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Return to acting")]

After an absence from acting of several years, in 1981 Fox appeared on television in the _[Play for Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Play\_for\_Today "Play for Today")_ "Country" by [Trevor Griffiths](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Griffiths "Trevor Griffiths"), a comedy drama set against the 1945 UK parliamentary elections. On film he starred in [Stephen Poliakoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Poliakoff "Stephen Poliakoff")'s _[Runners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Runners\_(film) "Runners (film)")_ (1983),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5)_[A Passage to India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Passage\_to\_India\_(film) "A Passage to India (film)")_ (1984),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) and _[Comrades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comrades\_(1986\_film) "Comrades (1986 film)")_ (1986).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) He played [Anthony Blunt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Blunt "Anthony Blunt") in the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC") play by [Alan Bennett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Bennett "Alan Bennett"), _[A Question of Attribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Question\_of\_Attribution "A Question of Attribution")_ (1992).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-tv-5) He also portrayed the character of Lord Holmes in _[Patriot Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patriot\_Games "Patriot Games")_ (1992), as well as Colonel Ferguson in _[Farewell to the King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farewell\_to\_the\_King "Farewell to the King")_ (1989) and the Nazi-sympathising aristocrat Lord Darlington in _[The Remains of the Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Remains\_of\_the\_Day\_(film) "The Remains of the Day (film)")_ (1993).

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Fox&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Fox married Mary Elizabeth Piper in September 1973, with whom he has five children, including [Laurence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Fox "Laurence Fox") and [Jack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Fox_(actor) "Jack Fox (actor)"). Piper died at their home on 19 April 2020.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-foxes-2)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-telegraph_241195-15)

Through his daughter Lydia, Fox's son-in-law is actor [Richard Ayoade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Ayoade "Richard Ayoade").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-telegraph_20170623-16) His former daughter-in-law is actress [Billie Piper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billie_Piper "Billie Piper"), who was married to his son Laurence from 2007 to 2016.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-BBC_News-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox#cite_note-itv_20160512-18)

# Gandhi (movie) facts for kids

[Kids Encyclopedia Facts](https://kids.kiddle.co/)

[![Image 3: Gandhi movie glasses](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/4/45/Gandhi_movie_glasses.jpg/300px-Gandhi_movie_glasses.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Gandhi_movie_glasses.jpg)

 Gandhi movie glasses

_**Gandhi**_ is a famous movie from 1982. It tells the true story of [Mohandas Gandhi](https://kids.kiddle.co/Mahatma_Gandhi "Mahatma Gandhi"), a very important leader from India. He worked hard for peace and freedom. This movie was made by teams from [Britain](https://kids.kiddle.co/Great_Britain "Great Britain"), [India](https://kids.kiddle.co/India "India"), and the [USA](https://kids.kiddle.co/United_States "United States").

The film was directed and produced by [Richard Attenborough](https://kids.kiddle.co/Richard_Attenborough "Richard Attenborough"). The main writer was [John Briley](https://kids.kiddle.co/John_Briley "John Briley"). Some parts were also written by [Steven Spielberg](https://kids.kiddle.co/Steven_Spielberg "Steven Spielberg").

## Contents

*   [About the Movie's Stars](https://kids.kiddle.co/Gandhi_(movie)#About_the_Movie.27s_Stars)
*   [When the Movie Came Out](https://kids.kiddle.co/Gandhi_(movie)#When_the_Movie_Came_Out)
*   [Awards and Recognition](https://kids.kiddle.co/Gandhi_(movie)#Awards_and_Recognition)
*   [A Dream Come True](https://kids.kiddle.co/Gandhi_(movie)#A_Dream_Come_True)
*   [See also](https://kids.kiddle.co/Gandhi_(movie)#See_also)

## About the Movie's Stars

The amazing actor [Ben Kingsley](https://kids.kiddle.co/Ben_Kingsley "Ben Kingsley") plays Gandhi in the movie. He did a fantastic job. Many other well-known actors are also in the film. These include [John Mills](https://kids.kiddle.co/John_Mills "John Mills"), [John Gielgud](https://kids.kiddle.co/John_Gielgud "John Gielgud"), and [Daniel Day-Lewis](https://kids.kiddle.co/Daniel_Day-Lewis "Daniel Day-Lewis"). You might also spot [Richard Griffiths](https://kids.kiddle.co/Richard_Griffiths "Richard Griffiths"), [Martin Sheen](https://kids.kiddle.co/Martin_Sheen "Martin Sheen"), [Nigel Hawthorne](https://kids.kiddle.co/Nigel_Hawthorne "Nigel Hawthorne"), and [John Ratzenberger](https://kids.kiddle.co/John_Ratzenberger "John Ratzenberger").

## When the Movie Came Out

_Gandhi_ was first shown in India on November 30, 1982. It then came to the United Kingdom on December 2, 1982. People in the United States could see it starting December 6, 1982. The movie was very popular. It earned over $52 million at the [box office](https://kids.kiddle.co/Box_office "Box office"). The movie cost about $13 million to make.

## Awards and Recognition

The movie _Gandhi_ won many big awards. It was nominated for eleven [Oscars](https://kids.kiddle.co/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards"). It ended up winning eight of them! This included the award for [Best Picture](https://kids.kiddle.co/Academy_Award_for_Best_Picture "Academy Award for Best Picture"). [Ben Kingsley](https://kids.kiddle.co/Ben_Kingsley "Ben Kingsley") won [Best Actor](https://kids.kiddle.co/Academy_Award_for_Best_Actor "Academy Award for Best Actor") for his role as Gandhi. [Richard Attenborough](https://kids.kiddle.co/Richard_Attenborough "Richard Attenborough") won [Best Director](https://kids.kiddle.co/Academy_Award_for_Best_Director "Academy Award for Best Director").

Besides the Oscars, _Gandhi_ also won other important awards. It received the Golden Globe Award for Best Picture. It also won the [BAFTA Award for Best Picture](https://kids.kiddle.co/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Film "BAFTA Award for Best Film"). These awards show how much people loved the movie.

## A Dream Come True

Director Richard Attenborough said that making the movie _Gandhi_ was his dream. He had wanted to tell Gandhi's story for a very long time. It was a very special project for him.

Michael James Radford (born 24 February 1946) is an English film director and screenwriter. He began his career as a documentary director and television comedy writer before transitioning into features in the early 1980s.

His best-known credits include the 1984 film adaptation of George Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four starring John Hurt and Richard Burton (in his final role), the Shakespeare adaptation The Merchant of Venice, the true crime drama White Mischief, and the 1994 Italian-language comedy drama Il Postino: The Postman, for which he won the BAFTA Awards for Best Direction and Best Film Not in the English Language, and earned Academy Award nominations for Best Director and Best Adapted Screenplay. ×

Michael James Radford (born 24 February 1946) is an English film director and screenwriter. He began his career as a documentary director and television comedy writer before transitioning into features in the early 1980s.

His best-known credits include the 1984 film adaptation of George Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four starring John Hurt and Richard Burton (in his final role), the Shakespeare adaptation The Merchant of Venice, the true crime drama White Mischief, and the 1994 Italian-language comedy drama Il Postino: The Postman, for which he won the BAFTA Awards for Best Direction and Best Film Not in the English Language, and earned Academy Award nominations for Best Director and Best Adapted Screenplay. ×

**Michael James Radford** (born 24 February 1946) is an English film director and screenwriter.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Radford#cite_note-NYT-1) He began his career as a documentary director and television comedy writer before transitioning into features in the early 1980s.

His best-known credits include the 1984 [film adaptation](link_33) of [George Orwell](link_8)'s _[Nineteen Eighty-Four](link_9)_ starring [John Hurt](link_10) and [Richard Burton](link_11) (in his final role), the [Shakespeare](link_12) adaptation _[The Merchant of Venice](link_13)_, the [true crime](link_14) drama _[White Mischief](link_15)_, and the 1994 Italian-language comedy drama _[Il Postino: The Postman](link_6)_, for which he won the [BAFTA Awards](link_16) for [Best Direction](link_5) and [Best Film Not in the English Language](link_7), and earned [Academy Award](link_17) nominations for [Best Director](link_18) and [Best Adapted Screenplay](link_19).

## Early life and career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Michael_Radford&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and career")]

Radford was born on 24 February 1946, in [New Delhi](link_20), [India](link_21), to a British father and an Austrian [Jewish](link_22) mother. He was educated at [Bedford School](link_23) before attending [Worcester College, Oxford](link_3). After teaching for a few years, he went to the [National Film and Television School](link_4), becoming a student there in its inaugural year.

Between 1976 and 1982, Radford worked as a documentary film maker, mostly on projects for the [BBC](link_24), covering subjects such as Scottish islanders on the [Isle of Lewis](link_25) in the [Outer Hebrides](link_26) who believe in the literal truth of the Bible: _The Last Stronghold of the Pure Gospel_; the soprano [Isobel Buchanan](link_27): _La Belle Isobel_; the singer songwriter [Van Morrison](link_28): _[Van Morrison in Ireland](link_29)_; and the self-explanatory _The Making of [The Pirates of Penzance](link_30)_. On the last two of these, Radford worked with the [cinematographer](link_31)[Roger Deakins](link_32), who would later shoot two of Radford's feature films; _[Nineteen Eighty-Four](link_33)_ and _[White Mischief](link_15)_. Another notable early work was _[Another Time, Another Place](link_34)_ (1983), a feature film set in [Scotland](link_35) during [World War II](link_36) and centred on a love story between a local woman and an [Italian](link_37)[POW](link_38).

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Michael_Radford&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

_**Nineteen Eighty-Four**_ (stylized as _**1984**_) is a 1984 British [dystopian film](link_17) written and directed by [Michael Radford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Radford "Michael Radford"), based on [George Orwell](link_4)'s [1949 novel](link_3). Starring [John Hurt](link_5), [Richard Burton](link_6), [Suzanna Hamilton](link_7) and [Cyril Cusack](link_8), it follows the life of [Winston Smith](link_18) (Hurt), a low-ranking civil servant in a war-torn London in [Oceania](link_19), a [totalitarian](link_20) superstate ruled by [Ingsoc](link_21) and its leader [Big Brother](link_22).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nineteen_Eighty-Four_(1984_film)#cite_note-6) Smith struggles to maintain his sanity and his grip on reality as the regime's overwhelming power and influence persecute [individualism](link_23) and individual thinking on both a political and a personal level.

_Nineteen Eighty-Four_ was Burton's last screen appearance; it was released two months after his death and is dedicated to him.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nineteen_Eighty-Four_(1984_film)#cite_note-tcmnotes-7) It was released in the United Kingdom on 10 October 1984 by [Virgin Films](link_13). It received positive reviews from critics, with many highlighted Deakins' cinematography and use of [bleach bypass](link_24). It was nominated for a [BAFTA Award for Best Art Direction](link_25), and won two [Evening Standard British Film Awards](link_26) for Best Film and Best Actor.

_**Another Time, Another Place**_ is a 1983 British [drama film](link_15) directed by [Michael Radford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Radford "Michael Radford") and starring [Phyllis Logan](link_5), Giovanni Mauriello and [Denise Coffey](link_6).[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Another_Time,_Another_Place_(1983_film)#cite_note-BFIsearch-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Another_Time,_Another_Place_(1983_film)#cite_note-3) The screenplay was based on the 1983 novel by [Jessie Kesson](link_3).[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Another_Time,_Another_Place_(1983_film)#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Another_Time,_Another_Place_(1983_film)#cite_note-5)

## Plot

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Another_Time,_Another_Place_(1983_film)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")]

In Scotland in 1943 during [World War II](link_16), Janie is a young Scottish housewife married to Dougal, who is 15 years older. Participating in a war rehabilitation program, the couple take in three Italian [prisoners of war](link_17) to work on their farm. Janie soon falls in love with one of the three, Luigi. She begins a secret relationship with Luigi that is doomed from the start.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Another_Time,_Another_Place_(1983_film)#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Another_Time,_Another_Place_(1983_film)#cite_note-7)

_**White Mischief**_ is a 1987 British [period](link_26)[crime drama](link_27) film directed and co-written by [Michael Radford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Radford "Michael Radford"). It dramatises the events of the [Happy Valley](link_28) murder case in [Kenya](link_29) in 1941, wherein Sir [Henry “Jock” Delves Broughton](link_30) was tried for the murder of [Josslyn Hay, 22nd Earl of Erroll](link_31). The film stars [Greta Scacchi](link_8), [Charles Dance](link_9), [Joss Ackland](link_10), [Sarah Miles](link_11), [Geraldine Chaplin](link_12), [Ray McAnally](link_13), [Murray Head](link_14), [John Hurt](link_15), and [Trevor Howard](link_16).

The screenplay is based on the non-fiction book _[White Mischief: The Murder of Lord Erroll](link_5)_ (1982), by [James Fox](link_6), which originated from a newspaper article published in 1969.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-whitemischief-6) Shooting took place on-location in Kenya and at [Shepperton Studios](link_32).

At the [42nd British Academy Film Awards](link_33), the film was nominated for [Best Actor in a Supporting Role](link_34) (for Joss Ackland) and [Best Costume Design](link_35).

The film came out around the same time as a BBC series set against the background of the same crime, _[The Happy Valley](link_36)_ (1987).

## Plot

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=White_Mischief_(film)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")]

Throughout the [Second World War](link_37), aristocrats in the [Kenya Colony](link_38)'s Happy Valley region often led hedonistic lifestyles of indulgence in alcohol, drugs, and extramarital relationships. On 24 January 1941, Josslyn Hay, the philandering Earl of Erroll, was found dead in his car in a secluded area, with his reputation for adulterous relationships preceding him.

One such married woman is [Diana Delves Broughton](link_39), the beautiful wife of Sir John Henry Delves Broughton, known as "Jock", who is thirty years her senior, with whom she has a pre-nuptial understanding that, should either of them fall in love with someone else, the other party would not impede that romance.

Diana has indeed succumbed to the charms of the Earl of Erroll,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-jongh-7) whose other lovers include the drug-addicted American heiress [Alice de Janzé](link_40) and the more reserved Nina Soames. The Earl is more serious about this affair than any of his earlier dalliances, and wants Diana to marry him. She is reluctant to leave what she thinks is the financial security of her marriage to formalise her relationship with Erroll (who has no funds or prospects), unaware that her husband is deep in debt. Privately humiliated but appearing to honour their agreement, Delves Broughton publicly toasts the couple's affair at the club in Nairobi, asking Erroll to bring Diana home at a specified time. Delves Broughton appears to be extremely intoxicated for the rest of the evening; once he is alone it is clear he was feigning drunkenness. After dropping off Diana, Erroll is shot dead in his car near the home of Delves Broughton, who is soon charged with the murder.

[Review by **Mark Cunliffe 🇵🇸**](link_70)[3](link_70)

I was actually going to score this three and a half but, a couple of hours now after watching it, the film continues to linger in my memory, haunting me. So, four stars it gets.

The directorial debut of Michael Radford (1984) Another Time, Another place is based on a novel by Jessie Kesson and is set in the remote, rural Scottish community of the Black Isle towards the end of WWII. The beautiful, fresh faced Phyllis Logan stars as Janie, a young housewife trapped in a loveless marriage to an older man, Dougal played by Paul Young. As part of a war rehabilitation program, Janie and Dougal welcome three Italian P.O.W.'s to work on their farm and Janie soon… [more](https://letterboxd.com/film/another-time-another-place-1983/#)

[![Image 8: lizzy deane](https://a.ltrbxd.com/resized/avatar/upload/5/5/5/6/5/4/shard/avtr-0-80-0-80-crop.jpg?v=8eaf1544fd)](https://letterboxd.com/punchdrunklizzy/ [link_71])

[Review by **lizzy deane**](link_72)[1](link_72)

Days of Airplane Angels. The greatest falling star over Scotland is that of feeling something that never had a locational origin. A feeling of being contented with someone on the either end, someone who feels just as much pain as you do. Maybe it should’ve been a different home, or a different forest, or a different era. It can’t be changed now.

[![Image 9: Paul Elliott](https://a.ltrbxd.com/resized/avatar/upload/1/1/5/4/3/8/5/shard/avtr-0-80-0-80-crop.jpg?v=dc6a740a91)](https://letterboxd.com/goliathreturns/ [link_73])

[Review by **Paul Elliott**](link_74)

_Another Time, Another Place_ emerges as a poignant, if somewhat uneven, exploration of love, loss, and the relentless march of time. Set against the backdrop of World War II, the film delves into the complexities of an illicit romance with a sensitivity and depth that resonates even decades after its release. Directed by Michael Radford, this cinematic piece offers a narrative enriched with emotional depth and historical context. At the heart of _Another Time, Another Place_ is the enchanting performance by Phyllis Logan, who plays Janie, a Scottish farm wife whose life is irrevocably changed by the arrival of Italian POW, Luigi, portrayed with equal parts charm and complexity by Giovanni Mauriello. Logan’s portrayal of Janie is a masterclass in… [more](https://letterboxd.com/film/another-time-another-place-1983/#)

[![Image 10: Mark Cunliffe 🇵🇸](https://a.ltrbxd.com/resized/avatar/upload/1/2/7/0/1/shard/avtr-0-80-0-80-crop.jpg?v=511a845ef7)](https://letterboxd.com/man_out_of_time/ [link_69])

[Review by **Mark Cunliffe 🇵🇸**](link_75)

Phyllis Logan ❤️

[Review by **Amoebrain**](link_77)

Phyllis Logan's smile is a tiny enamel sunrise

[![Image 12: C.C. Baxter](https://a.ltrbxd.com/resized/avatar/upload/1/7/1/8/1/4/shard/avtr-0-80-0-80-crop.jpg?v=3bc3d474e7)](https://letterboxd.com/cc_baxter/ [link_78])

[Review by **C.C. Baxter**](link_79)

Phyllis with that Wes Anderson hairdo

[![Image 13: Eurotrash](https://a.ltrbxd.com/resized/avatar/upload/3/9/3/9/5/8/shard/avtr-0-80-0-80-crop.jpg?v=97a298da5b)](https://letterboxd.com/eurotrash/ [link_80])

[Review by **Eurotrash**](link_81)

"Another Time, Another Place" spielt in Schottland während des Zweiten Weltkriegs: Drei italienische Kriegsgefangene werden dort zur Arbeit auf eine raue, abgelegene Farm geschickt. Weder die schottische Bevölkerung, noch die Kriegsgefangenen sind damit glücklich. Nur die junge, in ihrer Ehe eher unglückliche Janie widmet sich den Italienern etwas mehr, insbesondere dem charmanten Luigi und zwischen den Beiden entwickelt sich eine heimliche Romanze. Ob diese Liebe ein gutes Ende nehmen kann, trotz der widrigen Umstände, könnt ihr in diesem Film sehen.

Michael Radford nimmt sich hier viel Zeit für seine Figuren, was mich zu Beginn ein wenig abgeschreckt hat, denn es dauerte mir zu lang bis die Geschichte an Fahrt aufnimmt. Aufmuntern konnten mich die wirklich schönen Bilder der schottischen Landschaft und die zweite Hälfte des Films, der zwar kein Gute-Laune-Film ist, aber auch aufgrund seiner Bilder eine traurig-schöne Geschichte erzählt, die man bei entsprechender Stimmung sich mal geben kann.

[![Image 14: kev_n](https://a.ltrbxd.com/resized/avatar/upload/4/3/9/2/3/4/5/shard/avtr-0-80-0-80-crop.jpg?v=9921e1eaa0)](https://letterboxd.com/kev_n/ [link_82])

[Review by **kev_n**](link_83)

It’s always a shame when what could have been quiet, human story slips into melodrama to fulfill some phony dramatic structure. Some moments of inspiration, like cross-cutting our lead milking a cow while wrestling with daydreams of being surrounded by a group of men. Roger Deakins appears to be the main draw for viewers these days, and his composition is painterly, capturing both the bucolic beauty and stifling emptiness of rural life.

[![Image 15: Brian Lindsay](https://a.ltrbxd.com/resized/avatar/twitter/4/7/2/5/4/6/8/shard/http___pbs.twimg.com_profile_images_777278172412776448_GrfY0uNM-0-80-0-80-crop.jpg?v=8fe9fa77b9)](https://letterboxd.com/brianlindsay/ [link_84])

[Review by **Brian Lindsay**](link_85)

A beautifully unadorned portrait of infidelity as an act of illusory respite from tedium and loneliness. Finely crafted by Michael Radford with an eye to mood and character rather than incident or melodrama, the film is engaging and moving principally as a result of Phyllis Logan’s delicate portrayal. She deftly gives the material an emotional authenticity, captivating the viewer and carrying the quiet drama as a result.

[![Image 16: Saskia](https://a.ltrbxd.com/resized/avatar/upload/1/9/7/3/3/8/9/shard/avtr-0-80-0-80-crop.jpg?v=69ba512fa1)](https://letterboxd.com/agusyesbean/ [link_86])

[Review by **Saskia**](link_87)

Atmosphere is the most important element of this film. A sense of the monotony and boredom that Janie was faced with, and the vibrancy of Luigi in comparison. One of those films where the story seems to happen at the end rather than the whole way through, but such an interesting topic that I did not mind.

Quiet, slow and with some beautiful shots (Roger Deakins strikes again) Another Time, Another Place relies on the acting to elevate it. Phyllis Logan rightfully earned a BAFTA for this performance -the final scene in itself is worthy of that. I'm not even sure how I feel about the actual story/ conclusion, but it is something that I will not easily forget. Even just the look into rural Scottish life felt so fantastically authentic- and strikingly similar to the rural Ireland with which I am so familiar. Worth a watch.

[![Image 17: Luke](https://a.ltrbxd.com/resized/avatar/upload/1/0/1/4/9/9/shard/avtr-0-80-0-80-crop.jpg?v=e5f9a8c090)](https://letterboxd.com/lukecowan/ [link_88])

[Review by **Luke**](link_89)

bit like a Scots-Italian ‘Days of Heaven’ what with all the wheat and the clandestine love!

[youtu.be/qqTVSop144M](link_90)

[![Image 18: Iratak](https://s.ltrbxd.com/static/img/avatar80-CTtJ8HSs.png)](https://letterboxd.com/iratak/ [link_91])

[Review by **Iratak**](link_92)

Kinda wholesome in an "I cheated on my husband with an Italian soldier" sorta way. Husband cant satisfy his young beautiful Scottish wife ,so she develops wondering eye for the Italian soldier stationed nearby. All it takes is a proposition. I like the romance, ending feels a bit rushed.

[Review by **Eurotrash**](link_81)

"Another Time, Another Place" spielt in Schottland während des Zweiten Weltkriegs: Drei italienische Kriegsgefangene werden dort zur Arbeit auf eine raue, abgelegene Farm geschickt. Weder die schottische Bevölkerung, noch die Kriegsgefangenen sind damit glücklich. Nur die junge, in ihrer Ehe eher unglückliche Janie widmet sich den Italienern etwas mehr, insbesondere dem charmanten Luigi und zwischen den Beiden entwickelt sich eine heimliche Romanze. Ob diese Liebe ein gutes Ende nehmen kann, trotz der widrigen Umstände, könnt ihr in diesem Film sehen.

Michael Radford nimmt sich hier viel Zeit für seine Figuren, was mich zu Beginn ein wenig abgeschreckt hat, denn es dauerte mir zu lang bis die Geschichte an Fahrt aufnimmt. Aufmuntern konnten mich die wirklich schönen Bilder der schottischen Landschaft und die zweite Hälfte des Films, der zwar kein Gute-Laune-Film ist, aber auch aufgrund seiner Bilder eine traurig-schöne Geschichte erzählt, die man bei entsprechender Stimmung sich mal geben kann.

[Review by **kev_n**](link_83)

It’s always a shame when what could have been quiet, human story slips into melodrama to fulfill some phony dramatic structure. Some moments of inspiration, like cross-cutting our lead milking a cow while wrestling with daydreams of being surrounded by a group of men. Roger Deakins appears to be the main draw for viewers these days, and his composition is painterly, capturing both the bucolic beauty and stifling emptiness of rural life.

[![Image 15: Brian Lindsay](https://a.ltrbxd.com/resized/avatar/twitter/4/7/2/5/4/6/8/shard/http___pbs.twimg.com_profile_images_777278172412776448_GrfY0uNM-0-80-0-80-crop.jpg?v=8fe9fa77b9)](https://letterboxd.com/brianlindsay/ [link_84])

[Review by **Brian Lindsay**](link_85)

A beautifully unadorned portrait of infidelity as an act of illusory respite from tedium and loneliness. Finely crafted by Michael Radford with an eye to mood and character rather than incident or melodrama, the film is engaging and moving principally as a result of Phyllis Logan’s delicate portrayal. She deftly gives the material an emotional authenticity, captivating the viewer and carrying the quiet drama as a result.

[![Image 16: Saskia](https://a.ltrbxd.com/resized/avatar/upload/1/9/7/3/3/8/9/shard/avtr-0-80-0-80-crop.jpg?v=69ba512fa1)](https://letterboxd.com/agusyesbean/ [link_86])

[Review by **Saskia**](link_87)

Atmosphere is the most important element of this film. A sense of the monotony and boredom that Janie was faced with, and the vibrancy of Luigi in comparison. One of those films where the story seems to happen at the end rather than the whole way through, but such an interesting topic that I did not mind.

Quiet, slow and with some beautiful shots (Roger Deakins strikes again) Another Time, Another Place relies on the acting to elevate it. Phyllis Logan rightfully earned a BAFTA for this performance -the final scene in itself is worthy of that. I'm not even sure how I feel about the actual story/ conclusion, but it is something that I will not easily forget. Even just the look into rural Scottish life felt so fantastically authentic- and strikingly similar to the rural Ireland with which I am so familiar. Worth a watch.

### Synopsis

#### In a world of wife swapping, drugs and chocolate covered lobsters, murder seemed so uncivilised.

A millionaire past his prime and his young wife arrive in Kenya circa 1940 to find that the other affluent British expatriates are living large as the homefront gears up for war. They are busy swapping partners, doing drugs, and attending lavish parties and horse races. She begins a torrid affair with one of the bon vivants, and her husband finds out and confronts them. The husband and wife decide to break up peacefully, but the bon vivant is murdered and all the evidence points to the husband. ×

# White Mischief

[1987](link_14)
Directed by [Michael Radford](https://letterboxd.com/director/michael-radford/)

### Synopsis

#### In a world of wife swapping, drugs and chocolate covered lobsters, murder seemed so uncivilised.

A millionaire past his prime and his young wife arrive in Kenya circa 1940 to find that the other affluent British expatriates are living large as the homefront gears up for war. They are busy swapping partners, doing drugs, and attending lavish parties and horse races. She begins a torrid affair with one of the bon vivants, and her husband finds out and confronts them. The husband and wife decide to break up peacefully, but the bon vivant is murdered and all the evidence points to the husband. ×

# Nineteen Eighty-Four

[1984](link_10)
Directed by [Michael Radford](https://letterboxd.com/director/michael-radford/)

### Synopsis

#### George Orwell’s terrifying vision comes to the screen.

Imagine a world where absolute conformity rules, and word and thought, including loyalty to Big Brother is demanded. It’s the year 1984 and such a world exists. Divided into three vast states, whose inhabitants are dominated by all powerful governments, an illegal love affair begins. Soon, worker drone Winston becomes the target of a brain-washing campaign to force him back to conformity.

# FAQ

## The Merchant of Venice

Expand all below

Add to FAQ

* * *

Were any animals harmed in the making of this film? 

* * *

No (2:11:25)

Edit

* * *

* * *

What changes have been made from the original play? 

* * *

Two notable ones :  
  
1) Antonio, the merchant, is actually shown onscreen spitting at Shylock, the moneylender, at the very beginning, before the plot has even begun to develop. This serves to make him notably more unsympathetic than in the play, in which he treats Shylock more or less courteously until he is put on trial.  
2) The relationship between Bassanio and Antonio is clearly homosexual, while in the play it is more ambiguous, even innocent. There is even a moment in the film (not in the play) in which Portia indicates by a look and the tone of her voice that she clearly understands that Bassanio and Antonio are former lovers.

John Francis Lane was born on 1 December 1928 in Whitstable, Kent, England, UK. He was an actor and writer, known for [Black Tunnel (1986)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0090737/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk), [La piovra (1984)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0086779/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk) and [Another Time, Another Place (1983)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0036606/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk). He died in January 2018 in Cosenza, Calabria, Italy.

# Trivia

## 1984

Edit

In poor health during most of the filming, [Richard Burton](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000009/?ref_=tttrv_tr) had great difficulty remembering his lines and sometimes had to film a scene dozens of times before he could get it right. The scene in O'Brien's apartment where he is talking to Winston about Goldstein's book took a record of 41 takes for Burton to say his speech without fumbling his lines.

Helpful•400 4

Many of the scenes were shot on the days noted in Winston Smith's diary. The scene where Smith enters his apartment and writes in his diary, dating the entry April 4, 1984, was filmed on April 4, 1984.

Helpful•523 9

This was [Richard Burton](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000009/?ref_=tttrv_tr)'s final movie before his death on August 5, 1984, at the age of fifty-eight.

Helpful•339 7

The movie was filmed during April, May, and June 1984. The closing credits declare that "This film was photographed in and around London during the period April-June 1984, the exact time and setting imagined by the author ([George Orwell](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000567/?ref_=tttrv_tr))."

Helpful•445 12

Director [Michael Radford](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0705535/?ref_=tttrv_tr) and cinematographer [Roger Deakins](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0005683/?ref_=tttrv_tr) originally wanted to shoot this movie in black and white, but the financial backers of the production, Virgin Films, opposed this idea. Instead, Deakins used a film processing technique called bleach bypass to create the distinctive washed-out look of the movie's color visuals. This movie is a rare example of the technique being done on every release print, rather than the inter-negative or inter-positive; as the silver is retained in the print, and the lab is unable to reclaim the silver, so the cost is higher, but the retained silver gives a depth to the projected image. The 2003 DVD release (the only release to restore [Dominic Muldowney](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0611766/?ref_=tttrv_tr)'s full musical score) was mastered from the original negatives (not a release print), and thus inadvertently restored the movie's original color saturation.

Helpful•274 7

**Jonathan Gems** (born 1952, in [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London")) is a British playwright and screenwriter mostly known for his work on _[Mars Attacks!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars\_Attacks! "Mars Attacks!")_ (1996), directed by [Tim Burton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Burton "Tim Burton").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_Gems#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_Gems#cite_note-2) He also wrote the film's [novelization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Novelization "Novelization"). His well known work includes a screenplay for an adaptation of [George Orwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Orwell "George Orwell")'s novel _[1984](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nineteen\_Eighty-Four "Nineteen Eighty-Four")_ and _Mars Attacks Memoirs_, a book of interviews about working with Tim Burton behind the scenes of _Mars Attacks!_.

The son of the playwright [Pam Gems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pam_Gems "Pam Gems"),[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_Gems#cite_note-3) Gems wrote a number of plays for theatres on the London fringe before gradually turning to screenwriting.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_Gems#cite_note-4) As well as _Mars Attacks!_, Gems did uncredited rewrite work on _[Batman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batman\_(1989\_film) "Batman (1989 film)")_ (1989). Gems has written unproduced scripts for Burton, including a _[Beetlejuice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beetlejuice "Beetlejuice")_ (1988) sequel titled _Beetlejuice Goes Hawaiian_; an updating of [Edgar Allan Poe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Allan_Poe "Edgar Allan Poe")'s "[The Fall of the House of Usher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fall_of_the_House_of_Usher "The Fall of the House of Usher")" set in [Burbank, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burbank,_California "Burbank, California"); _[The Hawkline Monster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hawkline\_Monster:\_A\_Gothic\_Western#Adaptations "The Hawkline Monster: A Gothic Western")_, a cowboy/monster movie that was to star [Clint Eastwood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clint_Eastwood "Clint Eastwood") and [Jack Nicholson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Nicholson "Jack Nicholson"); and _Go Baby Go_, a beach movie in the style of films by [Russ Meyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russ_Meyer "Russ Meyer").

**Cyril James Cusack**[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyril_Cusack#cite_note-filmr-1) (26 November 1910 – 7 October 1993) was an Irish[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyril_Cusack#cite_note-nytimes.com-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyril_Cusack#cite_note-3) stage and screen actor with a career that spanned more than 70 years. During his lifetime, he was considered one of Ireland's finest thespians,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyril_Cusack#cite_note-4) and was renowned for his interpretations of both classical and contemporary theatre, including [Shakespearean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Shakespeare "William Shakespeare") roles as a member of the [Royal Shakespeare Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Shakespeare_Company "Royal Shakespeare Company"), and over 60 productions for the [Abbey Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abbey_Theatre "Abbey Theatre"), of which he was a lifelong member. In 2020, Cusack was ranked at number 14 on _[The Irish Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Irish\_Times "The Irish Times")_' list of Ireland's greatest film actors.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyril_Cusack#cite_note-5)

Born to Irish and English parents in South Africa and raised in [County Tipperary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_Tipperary "County Tipperary"), Cusack dropped out of law school to join the Abbey Theatre and remained with the company for 13 years, acting in over 60 plays. In London, he performed with the [Royal Shakespeare Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Shakespeare_Company "Royal Shakespeare Company") and the [Royal National Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_National_Theatre "Royal National Theatre"), and later founded his own company which toured across Europe. Making his film debut at age 8, Cusack worked with many notable directors, including [Powell and Pressburger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Powell_and_Pressburger "Powell and Pressburger"), [Franco Zeffirelli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franco_Zeffirelli "Franco Zeffirelli"), [François Truffaut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fran%C3%A7ois_Truffaut "François Truffaut"), [Carol Reed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carol_Reed "Carol Reed"), [Peter Brook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Brook "Peter Brook"), [Peter Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Hall_(director) "Peter Hall (director)"), [Fred Zinnemann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fred_Zinnemann "Fred Zinnemann"), [Christine Edzard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christine_Edzard "Christine Edzard") and [Anthony Harvey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Harvey "Anthony Harvey"). He co-starred opposite [Richard Burton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Burton "Richard Burton") several times, who once commended Cusack's acting as "always himself and yet always totally different". Fluent in both English and Irish, Cusack had a starring role in the first Irish-language feature film, [_Poitín_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poit%C3%ADn_(film) "Poitín (film)") (1978).

He was the patriarch of the Irish Cusack acting family, as the father of [Sinéad Cusack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sin%C3%A9ad_Cusack "Sinéad Cusack"), [Sorcha Cusack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sorcha_Cusack "Sorcha Cusack"),
