#### [Idle hands](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0094317/reviews/?featured=rw3380075&ref_=tt_ururv_c_2_hd)

Although I wouldn't say this is a great movie, it is definitely an entertaining one.  
  
The film tells the mostly true story of the fairly outrageous goings on amongst upper class Britons in Kenya during WW2. If the film does anything, it captures that outrageous spirit perfectly.  
  
Aging Sir John Henry Delves Broughton (Joss Ackland) leaves war-torn England with his beautiful young wife, Diana (Greta Scacchi), to oversee his properties in British Kenya. They join other ex-pat aristocrats in the incongruously named Happy Valley community. Although cocooned from the war in Europe, the denizens of the valley are completely at the mercy of the boredom generated by their privileged lifestyles, and their overheated libidos.  
  
They joyously encourage new arrivals to cheat on their partners, and then just as joyously inform the other halves about what is going on. Broughton begins to realise that he has something more disturbing than German bombs and falling commodity prices to worry about when Diana begins an open affair with Josslyn Hay, the Earl of Erroll (Charles Dance).  
  
Eventually it all ends in tears, murder and suicide.  
  
The film was not successful at the box office, and it's hard to pick just what put people off. However there is a fair amount of nudity in the film, which I think still tends to alienate mainstream audiences. Maybe the whole thing sounded too unsavoury - Diana is irresistible to males, especially older ones with even Trevor Howard's character peeping at her in the bath. There isn't anyone in the story whose intentions are strictly honourable.  
  
But with that said, the performances are fascinating. Joss Ackland is superb; we feel his humiliation as the virile Erroll offers Diana what he can't.  
  
The 1940's probably weren't the most flattering period for fashions, however Greta Scacchi looks stunning in them - she reminded me of Lana Turner in "The Postman Always Rings Twice".  
  
Charles Dance exudes an element of danger, much like Vincent Cassel. Tall and lithe, he wears black tie beautifully, but when he strips down you see how fit and agile he is - not a man to be trifled with.  
  
"White Mischief" has a certain pace and style and glides by easily. It stays in the memory, and is a long way from being a bad movie.

#### [a shortened storyline taken from earlier film](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0094317/reviews/?featured=rw1401264&ref_=tt_ururv_c_3_hd)

The performances of Sarah Miles and John Hurt make this film worth watching; however it is disappointing that Michael Radford does not use the full storyline of the original film : "The Happy Valley" - made in 1987, nor is the source acknowledged in the credits. Other than that it is quite a good remake, but the original should not be missed, as the story continues for some length - indeed the end of "White Mischief" is about the halfway point of the story in "The Happy Valley". This is another of Radford's remakes that seemed to receive acclaim as if it were an original concept - just as his version of the tale of Pablo Neruda - "Il Postino" - was taken from the lesser known earlier film "Ardiente Pacientia" (Burning Patience) which for my money was the the better film.

#### [White Mischief](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0094317/reviews/?featured=rw0252274&ref_=tt_ururv_c_4_hd)

As a family member, related to the main character, Sir Jock obviously for myself, it was a very interesting piece to watch, having grown up with full knowledge of the story in its entirety.  
  
It was fairly accurate, although, typically, like any Hollywood film, some artistic licenses were granted. In fact, in real life, Sir Jock, a typical aristocrat of his time, had been in other troubles before, such as insurance fraud, and to this day I am somewhat surprised even with his titles, money, etc, he actually got away with this crime, for everyone strongly feels he did do it.  
  
"The Sixth Earl of Carnarvon, Lord Porchester, was a close friend of Sir Delves, and a horse-racing jockey. Upon hearing of Jock's acquittal, he sent the famous cable: 'HEARTY CONGRATULATIONS UNDERSTAND YOU WON A NECK CLEVERLY REGARDS PORCHEY'. "  
  
 I loved the film, loved the decadence, and from what I have been told, this was all very typical of its time in Happy Valley Kenya. I gather both the Queen, as well as Bill Wyman from the Rolling Stones, each called it their favorite film for that year. Anyone especially familiar with British life, humor, etc, would find this most interesting.  
  
SHELAGH DELVES BROUGHTON

_**The Golden Child**_ is a 1986 American [dark fantasy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dark_fantasy "Dark fantasy")[action comedy film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Action_comedy_film "Action comedy film") directed by [Michael Ritchie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Ritchie_(film_director) "Michael Ritchie (film director)"). The film stars [Eddie Murphy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eddie_Murphy "Eddie Murphy") as Chandler Jarrell, a Los Angeles social worker who is informed that he is "[The Chosen One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Chosen_One_(trope) "The Chosen One (trope)")", and is destined to save "The Golden Child", a kidnapped [Tibetan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tibetan_people "Tibetan people") boy with [mystical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mysticism "Mysticism") powers who is said to be the [savior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salvation "Salvation") of all humankind. Alongside Murphy, the film's cast includes [Charlotte Lewis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlotte_Lewis "Charlotte Lewis") and [Charles Dance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Dance "Charles Dance").

_The Golden Child_ was produced and distributed by [Paramount Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount_Pictures "Paramount Pictures")[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Golden_Child#cite_note-Maslin-5) and grossed a total of $79,817,937 at the United States domestic box office.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Golden_Child#cite_note-numbers-1)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Golden_Child#cite_note-mojo-6)

## Plot

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Golden_Child&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")]

In a remote temple in Tibet, a young boy – the Golden Child – demonstrates his mystical powers to the [monks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monk "Monk") of the [temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temple "Temple") by reviving a dead [eastern rosella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_rosella "Eastern rosella"), which becomes a constant companion and [familiar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Familiar_spirit "Familiar spirit"). A mysterious man, Sardo Numspa, has his men break into the temple, slaughter the monks, and abduct the boy.

A young woman, [Kee Nang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kee_Nang "Kee Nang"), watches a [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles") TV show in which independent [social worker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_worker "Social worker") and [private detective](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Private_detective "Private detective") Chandler Jarrell talks about a missing girl named Cheryll Mosley. Kee informs him of the kidnapping of the Golden Child and that he is the "chosen one" who will save the Child. Chandler does not take this seriously, even after a bird begins following him and he sees an [astral projection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astral_projection "Astral projection") of the Child. The next day, Cheryll is found dead near an abandoned house smeared with Tibetan [graffiti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graffiti "Graffiti") and a pot full of blood-soaked oatmeal. Kee reveals to Chandler that this house was a holding place for the Child and introduces him to Doctor Hong, a mystic expert, and Kala (a creature half dragon, half woman).

Chandler and Kee track down a [motorcycle gang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outlaw_motorcycle_club "Outlaw motorcycle club"), the Yellow Dragons, which Cheryll had joined, and [Chinese restaurant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_restaurant "Chinese restaurant") owner Tommy Tong, a henchman of Numspa, to whom Cheryll had been "sold" for her blood, a way to make the Child vulnerable to earthly harm. However, Tong is killed by Numspa as a potential traitor. Still not taking the case too seriously, Chandler is drawn by Numspa into a [controlled dream](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucid_dream "Lucid dream"). Numspa presents his demands: the Ajanti Dagger (a mystic weapon capable of killing the Child) in exchange for the boy. Chandler agrees to help, and he and Kee spend the night together.

Chandler and Kee travel to [Tibet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tibet "Tibet"), where Chandler is swindled by an [amulet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amulet "Amulet") seller, later revealed as the High [Priest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Priest "Priest") of the temple where the dagger is kept hidden (and, subsequently, Kee's father). To obtain the knife, Chandler has to pass a test: an [obstacle course](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obstacle_course "Obstacle course") in a bottomless cavern whilst carrying a glass of water without spilling a drop. With luck and wits, he recovers the blade and brings it into the United States.

That night, Numspa and his henchmen attack Chandler and Kee. The Ajanti Dagger is lost to the villains, and Kee takes a crossbow bolt meant for Chandler, dying in his arms while confessing her love for him. Doctor Hong and Kala offer him hope: as long as the sun shines upon Kee, the Child might be able to save her. With the help of the Child's familiar, Chandler locates Numspa's hideout, retrieves the dagger with the help of Til, one of Numspa's men converted to good by the Child, and frees the boy. When Chandler confronts Numspa, he reveals himself as a winged demon. Chandler and the Child escape, only to be trapped inside a warehouse. Chandler loses the dagger when the warehouse collapses.

Chandler and the Child head to Doctor Hong's shop, where Kee is being kept. Numspa attacks Chandler, but the amulet the Old Man sold Chandler protects him, then blasts the dagger from Numspa's hand. The Child uses his magic to place the dagger back into Chandler's hands, and Chandler stabs Numspa, destroying him. The Child then uses the last rays of sunlight and his powers to bring Kee back from the dead. The three later take a walk discussing the Child's return to Tibet.

## Production

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Golden_Child&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Production")]

[Dennis Feldman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dennis_Feldman "Dennis Feldman"), a professional photographer whose only writing credit was _[Just One of the Guys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Just\_One\_of\_the\_Guys "Just One of the Guys")_, wrote a script called _The Rose of Tibet_, which he planned as "a [Raymond Chandler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raymond_Chandler "Raymond Chandler") movie with supernatural elements."[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Golden_Child#cite_note-Starlog-7) It attracted Hollywood's attention and after a bidding war [Paramount Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount_Pictures "Paramount Pictures") purchased the script for $330,000.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Golden_Child#cite_note-8) Feldman had intended it to be a detective story rather than a comedy and thought of [Mel Gibson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mel_Gibson "Mel Gibson") for the lead role.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Golden_Child#cite_note-Cormier-9)[John Carpenter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Carpenter "John Carpenter") was offered the chance to direct the film, but he preferred to instead work on _[Big Trouble in Little China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big\_Trouble\_in\_Little\_China "Big Trouble in Little China")_ (1986) starring [Kurt Russell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Russell "Kurt Russell").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Golden_Child#cite_note-Cormier-9) Murphy met with [George Miller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Miller_(filmmaker) "George Miller (filmmaker)") to direct the film.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Golden_Child#cite_note-10)

J. L. Reate, the actor who played the Golden Child, the male titular character, was actually a girl: Jasmine Lauren Reate, who was six years old when filming began. This was her only theatrical performance,[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Golden_Child#cite_note-11) but she wound up in the movie industry anyway: as of 2019, Reate was executive director of events at the [Toronto Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto_Film_Festival "Toronto Film Festival").

For special effects, the team used CGI,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Golden_Child#cite_note-filmsite13-12) as well as traditional [stop motion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stop_motion "Stop motion") and [go motion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Go_motion "Go motion").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Golden_Child#cite_note-13)

[Alan Silvestri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Silvestri "Alan Silvestri") (_[Back to the Future](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Back\_to\_the\_Future "Back to the Future")_) was originally sought to provide the film's score, but turned the project down. Paramount then turned to [John Barry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Barry_(composer) "John Barry (composer)"), who had just come off his award-winning score for _[Out of Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Out\_of\_Africa\_(film) "Out of Africa (film)")_. Barry composed a score for the film. However, during post-production, Barry also left the project, when both differences with the producers and [test screening](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Test_screening "Test screening") feedback presented considerable challenges for the composer.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Golden_Child#cite_note-Friendly-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Golden_Child#cite_note-afi-3) The test audience reaction led the producers to replace Barry's score with a second score, by [Michel Colombier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michel_Colombier "Michel Colombier") that, in contrast to Barry's work, was mostly "[synthpop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synthpop "Synthpop")" (although there were some brief orchestral passages throughout). Some of Barry's [musical cues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musical_cue "Musical cue") remain in the final cut of the film and one track, "Wisdom of the Ages", appeared on the first [soundtrack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soundtrack_album "Soundtrack album") release issued by [Capitol Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capitol_Records "Capitol Records").

In 2011, La-La Land Records released a limited-edition 3-CD soundtrack set containing the entirety of both Barry's mostly unused score (on disc one), and Colombier's final theatrical score (on disc two), in addition to an exclusive Barry-composed song, sung by emerging composer [Randy Edelman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randy_Edelman "Randy Edelman"). The songs that had been released on Capitol's first soundtrack in 1986 were also featured in the set. A stand-alone release of only Barry's original score was issued by La-La Land in 2026.

## Reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Golden_Child&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Reception")]

### Box office

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Golden_Child&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Box office")]

Released in December 1986, _The Golden Child_ was a box office success.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Golden_Child#cite_note-14) It earned US$79,817,937[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Golden_Child#cite_note-mojo-6) in the United States alone, making it the eighth biggest film of the year. "My pictures make their money back," [Eddie Murphy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eddie_Murphy "Eddie Murphy") remarked in 1989. "No matter how I feel, for instance, about _The Golden Child_ – which was a piece of shit – the movie made more than $100 million. So who am I to say it sucks?"[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Golden_Child#cite_note-Zehme-15) After _The Golden Child_, Murphy would participate in the writing of many of his films.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Despite its commercial success, the film did not meet Paramount's expectations when compared to Murphy's previous film, _[Beverly Hills Cop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beverly\_Hills\_Cop "Beverly Hills Cop")_ (1984), which grossed $234,760,478 at the US box office.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Golden_Child#cite_note-16)

### Critical response

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Golden_Child&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Critical response")]

On [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"), the film has an approval rating of 21% based on 28 reviews, with an average rating of 4.4/10.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Golden_Child#cite_note-17) On [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"), the film has a score of 37 out of 100, based on reviews from 12 critics, indicating "generally unfavorable reviews".[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Golden_Child#cite_note-18) Audiences surveyed by [CinemaScore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CinemaScore "CinemaScore") gave the film an average grade of "B" on an A+ to F scale.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Golden_Child#cite_note-19)

[Roger Ebert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Ebert "Roger Ebert") of _[Chicago Sun-Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago\_Sun-Times "Chicago Sun-Times")_ gave the film three out of four stars, and stated: "_The Golden Child_ may not be the Eddie Murphy movie we were waiting for, but it will do. It is funnier, more assured and more tailored to Murphy than _Beverly Hills Cop_ and it shows a side of his comic persona that I don't think has been much appreciated: his essential underlying sweetness. Murphy's comedy is not based on hurt and aggression, but on affection and an understanding that comes from seeing right through the other characters."[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Golden_Child#cite_note-20)

In his _[TV Movies and Video Guide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonard\_Maltin's\_Movie\_Guide "Leonard Maltin's Movie Guide")_, [Leonard Maltin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonard_Maltin "Leonard Maltin") cited the film as a BOMB (his lowest possible rating): "A top candidate for the worst megahit of all time...[Charlotte Lewis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlotte_Lewis "Charlotte Lewis") gives a wooden performance even for an ex-model; entire reels go by with hardly a chuckle. A box-office smash - but have you ever met anyone who says they liked it?"[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Golden_Child#cite_note-21)[Janet Maslin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janet_Maslin "Janet Maslin") of _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_ seemed to agree, describing the picture as a "comedy without laughs".[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Golden_Child#cite_note-Maslin-5)

Writer [Dennis Feldman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dennis_Feldman "Dennis Feldman") was disappointed with the film and thought they should have taken the script more seriously "but instead, everybody wanted to make an Eddie Murphy comedy" and was critical of director [Michael Ritchie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Ritchie_(film_director) "Michael Ritchie (film director)") "it's not what the director should have done—and he didn't even do it that well, either."[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Golden_Child#cite_note-Starlog-7)[Charles Dance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Dance "Charles Dance") (who played the villain Sardo Numspa) said: "I thought I'd quite like to do a film with Eddie Murphy because he makes me laugh. The character was villainous, but he was a comic villain as far as I was concerned, and I hadn't done a film like that before. I don't think as an actor you should back off from any experience, so I thought, 'OK, we'll try this.' And I did it, and I know that it's played over and over again and a lot of devotees of that kind of thing say it's their favorite film. It was fun. I enjoyed doing it."[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Golden_Child#cite_note-22)

The film was nominated for [best fantasy film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturn_Award_for_Best_Fantasy_Film "Saturn Award for Best Fantasy Film") at the [Saturn Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturn_Awards "Saturn Awards").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Golden_Child#cite_note-23)

# Trivia

## White Mischief

Edit

The producers wanted to fire [Trevor Howard](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0002145/?ref_=tttrv_tr) from this movie, due to his alcoholism, but [Sarah Miles](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0587234/?ref_=tttrv_tr) insisted he should stay.

The BBC television drama, [The Happy Valley (1986)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0093694/?ref_=tttrv_tr), covering the same subject matter, was broadcast on September 6, 1987, within the same year of this movie debuting in theaters.

Helpful•12 0

The closing credits legal disclaimer reads: "The story of this film is inspired by events which took place in Kenya in 1940 and 1941. The film does not purport to be an accurate representation of either the characters concerned, or the events that took place."

Helpful•16 1

Only career nude scene for Jacqueline Pearce. She talked about her audition process for this film in a 1991 TV Zone interview. Her agent had called her saying the producer Mike Radford and casting director Mary Selway wanted to see her, but since the role required nudity, they also wanted to see her naked. Pearce said it was no problem. When she arrived for the audition, all she wore were black stockings, a pair of high heeled shoes, and a full length mink. She walked into Radford's office, dropped the mink, stood before him and Selway stark naked, and said, "What do you think of that lot?" Radford hired her on the spot.

Helpful•9 0

Many movie posters featured a long blurb that read: "In England they were the elite, but bound by rules of society. In Kenya there were no rules, only glamour, decadence . . . and murder."

_**White Mischief**_ is a non-fiction book by British journalist [James Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox_(journalist) "James Fox (journalist)"), first published in hardback by [Jonathan Cape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_Cape "Jonathan Cape") in 1982 and in paperback in 1984 by [Penguin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penguin_Books "Penguin Books").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(novel)#cite_note-catalogue-1) The book is an account of the unsolved murder in 1941 of [Josslyn Hay, 22nd Earl of Erroll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josslyn_Hay,_22nd_Earl_of_Erroll "Josslyn Hay, 22nd Earl of Erroll"), a British expatriate in [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya"). The title is a pun on the title of [Evelyn Waugh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evelyn_Waugh "Evelyn Waugh")'s novel _[Black Mischief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black\_Mischief "Black Mischief")_ (1932). The book was adapted as a [film of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film) "White Mischief (film)") in 1987.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(novel)#cite_note-imdb-2)

## Synopsis

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=White_Mischief_(novel)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Synopsis")]

Part novel and part journalistic report, the book is divided into two distinct sections.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(novel)#cite_note-wordpress-3) Initially presented as a classic murder mystery, the first part of the story focuses on the dissolute lifestyles of the wealthy elite in colonial Kenya. Casual affairs, wife-swapping, habitual drunkenness and cocaine abuse were all common. The main protagonists are the victim, [Josslyn Hay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josslyn_Hay "Josslyn Hay"), a handsome womanising aristocrat; his beautiful married lover Lady [Diana Broughton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diana_Caldwell "Diana Caldwell"); and Diana’s much older husband Sir Delves Broughton. Although the identity of the murderer has never been discovered, the author claims to have found new evidence pointing to Sir Delves, and the second part of the book concentrates on the author’s investigations and his interviews with surviving participants in the drama, both in Kenya and in the United Kingdom.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(novel)#cite_note-goodreads-4)

## Film adaptation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=White_Mischief_(novel)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Film adaptation")]

_[White Mischief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White\_Mischief\_(film) "White Mischief (film)")_, released in 1987, was directed by [Michael Radford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Radford "Michael Radford"), and stars [Charles Dance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Dance "Charles Dance"), [Greta Scacchi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greta_Scacchi "Greta Scacchi") and [Joss Ackland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joss_Ackland "Joss Ackland").

_**For Your Eyes Only**_ is a 1981 [spy film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spy_film "Spy film"), the twelfth film in the [_James Bond_ franchise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_James_Bond_films "List of James Bond films") produced by [Eon Productions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eon_Productions "Eon Productions"), and the fifth to star [Roger Moore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Moore "Roger Moore") as the fictional [MI6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_Intelligence_Service "Secret Intelligence Service") agent [James Bond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portrayal_of_James_Bond_in_film "Portrayal of James Bond in film"). The film also co-stars [Carole Bouquet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carole_Bouquet "Carole Bouquet"), [Chaim Topol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chaim_Topol "Chaim Topol"), [Lynn-Holly Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lynn-Holly_Johnson "Lynn-Holly Johnson") and [Julian Glover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julian_Glover "Julian Glover"), and marked the feature [directorial debut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Directorial_debut "Directorial debut") of [John Glen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Glen_(director) "John Glen (director)"), who had served as a film editor and [second unit director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_unit_director "Second unit director") on previous films in the series.

The film was written by [Richard Maibaum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Maibaum "Richard Maibaum") and [Michael G. Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_G._Wilson "Michael G. Wilson"). Although the script is principally based on two [Ian Fleming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Fleming "Ian Fleming") short stories, "[For Your Eyes Only](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(short_story_collection)#%22For_Your_Eyes_Only%22 "For Your Eyes Only (short story collection)")" and "[Risico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(short_story_collection)#%22Risico%22 "For Your Eyes Only (short story collection)")", some elements of the plot were also inspired by the novels _[Live and Let Die](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live\_and\_Let\_Die\_(novel) "Live and Let Die (novel)")_, _[Goldfinger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goldfinger\_(novel) "Goldfinger (novel)")_ and _[On Her Majesty's Secret Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/On\_Her\_Majesty's\_Secret\_Service\_(novel) "On Her Majesty's Secret Service (novel)")_. The film follows Bond as he attempts to locate a missile command system while becoming tangled in a web of deception spun by rival Greek smugglers along with Melina Havelock, a woman seeking to avenge the murder of her parents.

After the science-fiction-focused _[Moonraker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moonraker\_(film) "Moonraker (film)")_, the producers wanted a return to the style of the early Bond films and the works of 007 creator Fleming. _For Your Eyes Only_ followed a grittier, more realistic approach and a narrative theme of revenge and its consequences, rather than the fantasy narrative of _Moonraker_. Filming took place from September 1980 to February 1981, and locations included Greece, Italy and the United Kingdom, while underwater footage was shot in [the Bahamas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bahamas "The Bahamas"). [Sheena Easton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheena_Easton "Sheena Easton") performed the title theme song.

_For Your Eyes Only_ was released in the UK on 24 June 1981 and in the US two days later; it received a mixed critical reception. The film's reputation has improved over time, with reviewers praising the more serious tone in comparison to previous entries in the series, with others saying it was the best of Moore's films after _[The Spy Who Loved Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Spy\_Who\_Loved\_Me\_(film) "The Spy Who Loved Me (film)")_. The film was a financial success, generating $195.3 million worldwide.

_For Your Eyes Only_ was the final Bond film to be distributed solely by [United Artists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Artists "United Artists"); the company was absorbed by [Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer "Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer") soon after this film's release. It was followed by _[Octopussy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Octopussy "Octopussy")_ in 1983.

## Plot

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")]

The British information-gathering vessel _St Georges_, which holds the Automatic Targeting Attack Communicator (ATAC), the system used by the Ministry of Defence to co-ordinate the [Royal Navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Navy "Royal Navy")'s fleet of [Polaris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Polaris_programme "UK Polaris programme") submarines, is sunk after [trawling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trawling "Trawling") an old [naval mine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naval_mine "Naval mine") in the [Ionian Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ionian_Sea "Ionian Sea"). The British ask marine archaeologist Sir Timothy Havelock secretly to locate the _St Georges_. However, he and his wife are then murdered on their yacht (_Triana_) by Cuban hitman Hector Gonzales. Havelock's daughter [Melina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judy_Havelock "Judy Havelock") witnesses the murders, and vows revenge.

The head of the [KGB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KGB "KGB"), [General Gogol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Gogol "General Gogol"), also has learned of the fate of the _St Georges_ and has notified his contact in Greece. [MI6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MI6 "MI6") agent James Bond is ordered by the [Minister of Defence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Defence_(United_Kingdom) "Ministry of Defence (United Kingdom)"), [Sir Frederick Gray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sir_Frederick_Gray "Sir Frederick Gray"), and MI6 Chief of Staff [Bill Tanner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Tanner "Bill Tanner") to retrieve the ATAC before the Soviets do so, for the transmitter could order attacks by the submarines' [Polaris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UGM-27_Polaris "UGM-27 Polaris")[ballistic missiles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ballistic_missile "Ballistic missile"). Bond goes to Spain to learn who hired Gonzales.

While spying on Gonzales's [villa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villa "Villa"), Bond is captured by his men, but escapes as a crossbow bolt kills Gonzales. The assassin was Melina, who escapes with Bond. Aided by Bond, [Q](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Q_(James_Bond) "Q (James Bond)") uses the computerised Identigraph to identify the man Bond saw paying off Gonzales as Emile Leopold Locque and goes to Locque's possible base in [Cortina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cortina_d'Ampezzo "Cortina d'Ampezzo"), Italy. There, Bond meets his contact, Luigi Ferrara, and a well-connected Greek business magnate and intelligence informant, Aris Kristatos, who reveals that Locque is employed by Milos Columbo, known as "the Dove" in the Greek underworld, Kristatos's former [Greek resistance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greek_resistance "Greek resistance") partner during the [Second World War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_World_War "Second World War"). After Bond goes with Kristatos's [protégée](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prot%C3%A9g%C3%A9e "Protégée"), [figure skater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Figure_skater "Figure skater") Bibi Dahl, to a [biathlon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biathlon "Biathlon") course, a group of three men, which includes East German biathlete Eric Kriegler, chases Bond, trying to kill him. Bond escapes and goes with Ferrara to bid Bibi farewell in an ice rink, where he fends off another attempt on his life by three men in ice hockey gear. Ferrara is killed in Bond's car, with a dove pin in his hand. Bond then travels to [Corfu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corfu "Corfu") in pursuit of Columbo.

There, at the casino, Bond meets Kristatos and asks how to meet Columbo, not knowing that Columbo's men are secretly recording their conversation. After Columbo and his mistress, Countess Lisl von Schlaf, argue, Bond offers to escort her home with Kristatos's car and driver. The two spend the night together and the next morning, Lisl and Bond are ambushed on the beach and Lisl is killed by Locque, who mows her down in a beach buggy before speeding away. Bond is captured by Columbo's men before Locque can kill him; Columbo then tells Bond that Locque was actually hired by Kristatos, who is working for the KGB to retrieve the ATAC. Bond accompanies Columbo and his crew on a raid on one of Kristatos's [opium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opium "Opium")-processing warehouses in [Albania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Socialist_Republic_of_Albania "People's Socialist Republic of Albania"), where Bond uncovers naval mines similar to the one that sank the _St Georges_. After the base is destroyed, Bond chases Locque and kills him by shoving his car off a cliff while he is trapped inside.

Afterwards, Bond meets Melina, and they recover the ATAC from the wreckage of the _St Georges_, but Kristatos is waiting for them when they surface and takes the ATAC. The two escape an assassination attempt and discover Kristatos's [rendezvous](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/rendezvous "wikt:rendezvous") point when Melina's parrot, Max, repeats the phrase "ATAC to St Cyril's". Aided by Columbo and his men, Bond and Melina break into St Cyril's, an abandoned mountaintop monastery. Bond scales the peak and dispatches Apostis, a henchman of Kristatos. As Columbo confronts Kristatos, Bond kills Kriegler.

Bond retrieves the ATAC system and stops Melina from killing Kristatos after he surrenders. Kristatos prepares to kill Bond with a hidden [flick knife](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flick_knife "Flick knife"), but is killed by a knife thrown by Columbo; Gogol arrives by helicopter to collect the ATAC, but Bond throws it off the cliff, maintaining the relatively peaceful status quo, and Gogol departs in amused understanding. Bond and Melina later spend a romantic evening aboard her father's yacht while Melina's parrot fields a call from MI6 and [British Prime Minister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Prime_Minister "British Prime Minister")[Margaret Thatcher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Margaret_Thatcher "Margaret Thatcher").
