[John Hollis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Hollis "John Hollis") plays the bald villain in a wheelchair,[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPfeifferWorrall1998127-11) voiced by [Peter Marinker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Marinker "Peter Marinker").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-12) The character appears in the pre-credits sequence and is both unnamed and uncredited. The character contains a number of characteristics of [Ernst Stavro Blofeld](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernst_Stavro_Blofeld "Ernst Stavro Blofeld"),[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPfeifferWorrall1998127-11) but could not be identified as such because of the legal reasons surrounding the [_Thunderball_ controversy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thunderball_(novel)#Plagiarism_accusation_and_court_case "Thunderball (novel)") with [Kevin McClory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_McClory "Kevin McClory") claiming sole rights to the Blofeld character, a claim disputed by Eon.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-FOOTNOTESmith2002178-13)[Bob Simmons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Simmons_(stunt_man) "Bob Simmons (stunt man)"), who previously portrayed Bond in the [gun barrel sequences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gun_barrel_sequence "Gun barrel sequence") in the first three films and SPECTRE agent Colonel Jacques Bouvar in _[Thunderball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thunderball\_(film) "Thunderball (film)")_, cameos as another villain as Gonzales's henchman who falls victim to Bond's exploding [Lotus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lotus_Esprit "Lotus Esprit").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBarnesHearn2001138-9) Victor Tourjansky, the assistant director, has his third cameo in the _Bond_ films as a drinking tourist;[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-14) he is credited as part of the Ski Team for Stunts. [Charles Dance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Dance "Charles Dance") appears as Claus, Locque's right-hand man in the ski slope sequence, who is later killed by one of Columbo's frogmen while holding Bond at gunpoint after the beach chase where Locque kills Lisl. [Janet Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janet_Brown "Janet Brown") plays [Margaret Thatcher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Margaret_Thatcher "Margaret Thatcher"), the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, who appears in the closing scene alongside [John Wells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Wells_(satirist) "John Wells (satirist)") as her husband, [Denis Thatcher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denis_Thatcher "Denis Thatcher").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-15)

## Production

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Production")]

> We had gone as far as we could into space. We needed a change of some sort, back to the grass roots of Bond. We wanted to make the new film more of a thriller than a romp, without losing sight of what made Bond famous—its humour.

—John Glen[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-16)

[Ian Fleming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Fleming "Ian Fleming") wrote the original story "[For Your Eyes Only](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(short_story_collection) "For Your Eyes Only (short story collection)")" as an episode of a cancelled _James Bond_ television series at [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") in 1958.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-:2-8) Eon Productions originally intended to produce _For Your Eyes Only_ after [_The Spy Who Loved Me_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Spy_Who_Loved_Me_(film) "The Spy Who Loved Me (film)").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-:0-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-:1-18) However, after the success of _[Star Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star\_Wars\_(film) "Star Wars (film)")_ in 1977 the producers decided to produce _[Moonraker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moonraker\_(film) "Moonraker (film)")_ instead.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-19)_Moonraker_ was successful yet had been very expensive to produce, and shortly afterwards [United Artists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Artists "United Artists") suffered a major financial flop with [Michael Cimino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Cimino "Michael Cimino")'s _[Heaven's Gate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heaven's\_Gate\_(film) "Heaven's Gate (film)")_. This, along with the [early 1980s recession](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_1980s_recession "Early 1980s recession"), required _For Your Eyes Only_ to have a lower budget. _For Your Eyes Only_ marked a change in the make up of the production crew. The previous series directors [Terence Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terence_Young_(director) "Terence Young (director)"), [Guy Hamilton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guy_Hamilton "Guy Hamilton"), [Lewis Gilbert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lewis_Gilbert "Lewis Gilbert") and [Peter Hunt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_R._Hunt "Peter R. Hunt") were unable to direct because the studio could not afford to hire them, and [John Glen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Glen_(director) "John Glen (director)") was promoted from his duties as a [film editor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_editor "Film editor") to director, a position he would occupy for four subsequent films.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-:2-8)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-inside-20) Glen brought on much of his second-unit direction team from _The Spy Who Loved Me_ and _Moonraker_, including cinematographer [Alan Hume](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Hume "Alan Hume").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-:2-8) The transition in directors and lower budget resulted in a harder-edged directorial style, with less emphasis on gadgetry and large action sequences in huge arenas as was favoured by Gilbert in the previous two films.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-FOOTNOTECorkStutz2007299-21) Emphasis was placed on tension, plot and character in addition to a return to Bond's more serious roots,[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBenson1988226-22) whilst _For Your Eyes Only_ "showed a clear attempt to activate some lapsed and inactive parts of the Bond mythology."[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-FOOTNOTELindner200329-23)

The film was also a deliberate effort to bring the series more back to reality, following the success of _Moonraker_ in 1979.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-FOOTNOTECorkStutz2007292-24) As co-writer Michael G. Wilson pointed out, "If we went through the path of _Moonraker_ things would just get more outlandish, so we needed to get back to basics".[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-inside-20) To that end, the story that emerged was simpler, not one in which the world was at risk, but returning the series to that of a Cold War thriller;[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-inside-20) Bond would also rely more on his wits than gadgets to survive.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-wilson-25) Glen decided to symbolically represent it with a scene where Bond's [Lotus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lotus_Esprit_Turbo "Lotus Esprit Turbo") blows itself up and forces 007 to rely on Melina's more humble [Citroën 2CV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citro%C3%ABn_2CV "Citroën 2CV").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-inside-20) Since [Ken Adam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Adam "Ken Adam") was busy with _[Pennies from Heaven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennies\_from\_Heaven\_(1981\_film) "Pennies from Heaven (1981 film)")_, [Peter Lamont](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Lamont "Peter Lamont"), who had worked in the art department since _[Goldfinger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goldfinger\_(film) "Goldfinger (film)")_, was promoted to production designer. Following a suggestion of Glen, Lamont created realistic scenery, instead of the elaborate set pieces for which the series had been known.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-inside-20)[Elizabeth Waller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth_Waller "Elizabeth Waller"), an Emmy-winning costume designer with years of BBC experience, was brought on to design Bond's wardrobe.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-26)

### Writing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Writing")]

Before the project was postponed in favour of _Moonraker_, [Tom Mankiewicz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Mankiewicz "Tom Mankiewicz") had written a storyline and [Christopher Wood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Wood_(writer) "Christopher Wood (writer)") submitted a first draft in January 1978. However, their screenplay did not influence the final film.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-:0-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-:1-18) Richard Maibaum was once again the scriptwriter for the story, assisted by Michael G. Wilson.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBenson1988227-27) According to Wilson, the ideas from stories could have come from anyone as the outlines were worked out in committee that could include Broccoli, Maibaum, Wilson and [stunt coordinators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stunt_coordinator "Stunt coordinator").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBarnesHearn2001135-28) Much of the inspiration for the stories for the film came from two Ian Fleming short stories from the collection _For Your Eyes Only_: _[Risico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For\_Your\_Eyes\_Only\_(short\_story\_collection)#Risico "For Your Eyes Only (short story collection)")_ and _[For Your Eyes Only](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For\_Your\_Eyes\_Only\_(short\_story\_collection)#For\_Your\_Eyes\_Only "For Your Eyes Only (short story collection)")_.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-FOOTNOTESmith2002175-29) Another set-piece from the novel of _Live and Let Die_—the [keelhauling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keelhauling "Keelhauling")—which was unused in the film of the same name, was also inserted into the plot.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBarnesHearn2001135-28) Other ideas from Fleming were also used in _For Your Eyes Only_, such as the [Identigraph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facial_recognition_system "Facial recognition system") which comes from the novel _Goldfinger_, where it was originally called the "Identicast".[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBenson1988231-30) These elements from Fleming's stories were mixed with a [Cold War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_War "Cold War") story centred on the [MacGuffin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MacGuffin "MacGuffin") of the ATAC.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBenson1988227-27) An initial treatment for this film was submitted by [Ronald Hardy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Hardy "Ronald Hardy"), an English novelist and screenwriter, in 1979. Hardy's treatment included the involvement of a character named Julia Havelock whose parents were assassinated by a man named Gonzales.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-31)

The pre-title sequence of _For Your Eyes Only_ has been described as either "out-of place and disappointing"[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBenson1988227-27) or "roaringly enjoyable".[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-FOOTNOTESmith2002167-32) The scene was shot to introduce a potential new Bond to audiences, thus linking the new actor to elements from previous Bond films[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBarnesHearn2001135-28) (see [casting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#Casting), below).

The sequence begins with Bond laying flowers at the grave of his wife [Tracy Bond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tracy_Bond "Tracy Bond"), before a [Universal Exports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Exports "Universal Exports") helicopter picks him up for an emergency. Control of the helicopter is taken over by remote control by a bald man in a grey [Nehru jacket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nehru_jacket "Nehru jacket") with a white cat. This character is unnamed in either the film or the credits, although he looks and sounds like [Ernst Stavro Blofeld](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernst_Stavro_Blofeld "Ernst Stavro Blofeld") as played by [Donald Pleasence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Pleasence "Donald Pleasence") or [Telly Savalas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telly_Savalas "Telly Savalas").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBenson1988227-27) Director John Glen referred to the identity of the villain obliquely: "We just let people use their imaginations and draw their own conclusions... It's a legal thing".[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBarnesHearn2001137-4) Originally the character was going to be explicitly identified as Blofeld, but was deliberately not named due to copyright restrictions with [Kevin McClory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_McClory "Kevin McClory"), who owned the film rights to _[Thunderball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thunderball\_(novel) "Thunderball (novel)")_, which supposedly includes the character Ernst Stavro Blofeld, the organisation [SPECTRE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SPECTRE "SPECTRE"), and other material associated with the development of _Thunderball_.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-:2-8)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-33)[Eon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eon_Productions "Eon Productions") disputed McClory's ownership of the Blofeld character, but decided not to use him again: the scene was "a deliberate statement by Broccoli of his lack of need to use the character."[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-FOOTNOTESmith2002178-13)

Maibaum later said "We tried to return to the earlier films with _For Your Eyes Only_ but we didn't have Sean to make it real. And I was very disappointed with the way the love story was handled. The whole idea was that the great lover James Bond can't get to first base with this woman because she was so obsessed with avenging her parents' death. Nothing was ever done with it. It was as if the director didn't feel there was a love story there at all."[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-34)

### Casting

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Casting")]

Roger Moore had originally signed a three-film contract with Eon Productions, which covered his first three appearances (_[Live and Let Die](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live\_and\_Let\_Die\_(film) "Live and Let Die (film)")_ in 1973, _[The Man with the Golden Gun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Man\_with\_the\_Golden\_Gun\_(film) "The Man with the Golden Gun (film)")_ in 1974 and _[The Spy Who Loved Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Spy\_Who\_Loved\_Me\_(film) "The Spy Who Loved Me (film)")_ in 1977). Subsequent to this, the actor negotiated contracts on a film-by-film basis starting with _[Moonraker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moonraker\_(film) "Moonraker (film)")_ in 1979.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBarnesHearn2001135-28) Uncertainty surrounding his involvement in _For Your Eyes Only_, considering his age, led to other actors being considered to take over. The candidates included [Lewis Collins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lewis_Collins "Lewis Collins"), known in the UK for his portrayal of Bodie in _[The Professionals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Professionals\_(TV\_series) "The Professionals (TV series)")_; [Ian Ogilvy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Ogilvy "Ian Ogilvy"), known for his role as Simon Templar in _[Return of the Saint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Return\_of\_the\_Saint "Return of the Saint")_; [Michael Billington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Billington_(actor) "Michael Billington (actor)"), who previously appeared in _[The Spy Who Loved Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Spy\_Who\_Loved\_Me\_(film) "The Spy Who Loved Me (film)")_ as Agent XXX's ill-fated lover Sergei Barzov;[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-35) and [Michael Jayston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Jayston "Michael Jayston"), who had appeared as Quiller in the television series _[Quiller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quiller\_(TV\_series) "Quiller (TV series)")_.[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-36)[[c]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-40)[Timothy Dalton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timothy_Dalton "Timothy Dalton") was strongly considered for the role, but he disliked the direction the series was taking at the time, and he withdrew himself from contention. [[d]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-45)[[e]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-49)

[Bernard Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Lee "Bernard Lee") died of cancer on 16 January 1981, after filming began on _For Your Eyes Only_, but before he could film his scenes as [M](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M_(James_Bond) "M (James Bond)"), the head of MI6, as he had done in the previous eleven films of the series. Out of respect, no new actor was hired to assume the role as Broccoli refused to have the character recast and, instead, the script was re-written so that the character is said to be on leave, letting Chief of Staff Bill Tanner take over the role as acting head of MI6 and briefing Bond alongside the Minister of Defence.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPfeifferWorrall199898-50) This is only the second time M has been omitted from a Bond production, the first being the 1954 TV adaptation of _[Casino Royale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casino\_Royale\_(Climax!) "Casino Royale (Climax!)")_. Ironically, the original "For Your Eyes Only" short story dealt with Bond being given a personal mission by M, one of the few times in the Fleming canon that 007 did his superior a direct favour.

[Chaim Topol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chaim_Topol "Chaim Topol") was cast following a suggestion by Broccoli's wife Dana, while [Julian Glover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julian_Glover "Julian Glover") joined the cast as the producers felt he was stylish—Glover was even considered to play Bond at some point, but Michael G. Wilson stated that "when we first thought of him he was too young, and by the time of _For Your Eyes Only_ he was too old".[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-inside-20)

Italian actress [Ornella Muti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ornella_Muti "Ornella Muti") was considered for the movie, but she turned down the lead role (later given to [Carole Bouquet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carole_Bouquet "Carole Bouquet")) because her costume designer, [Wayne Finkelman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wayne_Finkelman?action=edit&redlink=1 "Wayne Finkelman (page does not exist)"), was not hired by the production.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-51)[Carole Bouquet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carole_Bouquet "Carole Bouquet") was a suggestion of United Artists publicist Jerry Juroe, and after Glen and Broccoli saw her in _[That Obscure Object of Desire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/That\_Obscure\_Object\_of\_Desire "That Obscure Object of Desire")_, they went to Rome to invite Bouquet for the role of Melina.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-glen-52)

### Filming

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Filming")]

[![Image 9: A yellow car drives down a grassy road.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7c/2cv_007.jpg/250px-2cv_007.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2cv_007.jpg)

The [Citroën 2CV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citro%C3%ABn_2CV "Citroën 2CV") used in the film

Production of _For Your Eyes Only_ began on 2 September 1980 in the [North Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Sea "North Sea"), with three days shooting exterior scenes with the _St Georges_.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-inside-20)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-acin-53) Although the previous film had been shot almost entirely outside of the United Kingdom, the new [Conservative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservative_Party_(UK) "Conservative Party (UK)") Prime Minister [Margaret Thatcher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Margaret_Thatcher "Margaret Thatcher")'s [tax cuts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tax_cut "Tax cut") allowed the shoot to return to Britain.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-:2-8) The interiors were shot later in [Pinewood Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinewood_Studios "Pinewood Studios"), as well as the ship's explosion, which was done with a miniature in Pinewood's tank on the [007 Stage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/007_Stage "007 Stage").[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-54) On 15 September [principal photography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principal_photography "Principal photography") started on Corfu at the Villa Sylva at Kanoni, above [Corfu Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corfu_Town "Corfu Town"),[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-FOOTNOTECorkStutz2007292-24) which acted as the location of the Spanish villa. Many of the local houses were painted white for [scenographic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scenography "Scenography") reasons.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-big-55) Glen opted to use the local slopes and olive trees for the chase scene between Melina's [Citroën 2CV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citro%C3%ABn_2CV "Citroën 2CV") and Gonzales's men driving [Peugeot 504s](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peugeot_504 "Peugeot 504").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-glen-52) The scene was shot across twelve days, with stunt driver [Rémy Julienne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R%C3%A9my_Julienne "Rémy Julienne")—who would remain in the series up until _[GoldenEye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GoldenEye "GoldenEye")_—driving the Citroën.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-56) Four 2CVs were used, with modifications for the stunts—all had more powerful [flat-four engines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flat-four_engine "Flat-four engine"), and one received a special revolving plate on its roof so it could rotate once it got turned upside down.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-57)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-58)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-59)

In October filming moved to other Greek locations, including [Meteora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meteora "Meteora") and the [Achilleion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Achilleion_(Corfu) "Achilleion (Corfu)").[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-locations-60) In November, the main unit moved to England, which included interior work in Pinewood, while the second unit shot underwater scenes in [the Bahamas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bahamas "The Bahamas"). On 1 January 1981, production moved to [Cortina d'Ampezzo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cortina_d'Ampezzo "Cortina d'Ampezzo") in Italy, where filming wrapped in February.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-inside-20) Filming locations in Cortina included the historic [Grand Hotel Miramonti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Hotel_Miramonti "Grand Hotel Miramonti").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-On_the_Tracks_of_007-61) Since it was not snowing in Cortina d'Ampezzo by the time of filming, the producers had to pay for trucks to bring snow from nearby mountains, which was then dumped in the city's streets.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-cortina-62)

Many of the underwater scenes, especially involving close-ups of Bond and Melina, were [faked on a dry soundstage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dry_for_wet "Dry for wet"). A combination of lighting effects, slow-motion photography, wind and bubbles added in post-production, gave the illusion of the actors being underwater.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-FOOTNOTECorkStutz2007292-24) Actress Carole Bouquet reportedly had a pre-existing health condition that prevented her from performing underwater stunt work.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-inside-20) Aquatic scenes were done by a team led by Al Giddings, who had previously worked on _[The Deep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Deep\_(1977\_film) "The Deep (1977 film)")_, and filmed in either Pinewood's tank on the 007 Stage or an underwater set built in the Bahamas. Production designer [Peter Lamont](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Lamont "Peter Lamont") and his team developed two working props for the [submarine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Submarine "Submarine") Neptune, as well as a mock-up with a fake bottom.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-63)

Roger Moore was reluctant to film the scene of Bond kicking a car, with Locque inside, over the edge of a cliff, saying that it "was Bond-like, but not Roger Moore Bond-like."[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-inside-20) Michael G. Wilson later said that Moore had to be persuaded to be more ruthless than he felt comfortable.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBarnesHearn2001137-4) Wilson also added that he and Richard Maibaum, along with John Glen, toyed with other ideas surrounding that scene, but ultimately everyone, even Moore, agreed to do the scene as originally written.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-inside-20)

[![Image 10: A monastery stands atop a large mountain.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5e/Meteora_Agios_Triadas_IMG_7632.jpg/250px-Meteora_Agios_Triadas_IMG_7632.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Meteora_Agios_Triadas_IMG_7632.jpg)

The [Monastery of the Holy Trinity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monastery_of_the_Holy_Trinity,_Meteora "Monastery of the Holy Trinity, Meteora") in [Meteora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meteora "Meteora") served as a location

For the Meteora shoots, a Greek bishop was paid to allow filming in the monasteries, but the uninformed [Eastern Orthodox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Orthodox "Eastern Orthodox") monks were mostly critical of production rolling in their installations. After a trial in the [Greek Supreme Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Civil_and_Criminal_Court_of_Greece "Supreme Civil and Criminal Court of Greece"), it was decided that the monks' only property were the interiors—the exteriors and surrounding landscapes were from the local government. In protest, the monks remained shut inside the monasteries during the shooting,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-inside-20)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-big-55) and tried to sabotage production as much as possible, hanging their washing out of their windows[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBarnesHearn2001138-9) and covering the principal monastery with plastic bunting and flags to spoil the shots, and placing oil drums to prevent the film crew from landing helicopters. The production team solved the problem with back lighting, [matte paintings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matte_painting "Matte painting") and building both a similar scenographic monastery on a nearby unoccupied rock, and a monastery set in Pinewood.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-acin-53)

Roger Moore said he had a great fear of heights, and to do the climbing in Greece, he resorted to moderate drinking to calm his nerves.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-inside-20) Later in that same sequence, [Rick Sylvester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Sylvester "Rick Sylvester"), a stuntman who had previously performed the pre-credits [ski jump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ski_jump "Ski jump") in _[The Spy Who Loved Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Spy\_Who\_Loved\_Me\_(film) "The Spy Who Loved Me (film)")_, undertook the stunt of Bond falling off the side of the cliff.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-stunts-64) The stunt was dangerous, since the sudden rope jerk at the bottom could be fatal. Special effects supervisor [Derek Meddings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derek_Meddings "Derek Meddings") developed a system that would dampen the stop, but Sylvester recalled that his nerves nearly got the better of him: "From where we were [shooting], you could see the local cemetery; and the box [to stop my fall] looked like a casket. You didn't need to be an English major to connect the dots." The stunt went off without a problem.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-inside-20)

Bond cameraman and professional skier [Willy Bogner Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willy_Bogner_Jr. "Willy Bogner Jr.") was promoted to director of a second unit involving ski footage.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-cortina-62) Bogner designed the ski chase on the [bobsleigh track of Cortina d'Ampezzo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eugenio_Monti_olympic_track "Eugenio Monti olympic track") hoping to surpass his work in both _On Her Majesty's Secret Service_ and _The Spy Who Loved Me_.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-inside-20) To allow better filming, Bogner developed both a system where he was attached to a [bobsleigh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bobsleigh "Bobsleigh"), allowing to film the vehicle or behind it,[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-stunts-64) and a set of skis that allowed him to ski forwards and backwards to get the best shots.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-FOOTNOTECorkStutz2007292-24) In February 1981, on the final day of filming the bobsleigh chase, one of the stuntmen driving a sleigh, 23-year-old Paolo Rigon, was killed when he became trapped under the bob. The incident, which took place a week after the [FIBT World Championships 1981](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIBT_World_Championships_1981 "FIBT World Championships 1981") where USA-1 bobsled driver [James Morgan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Morgan_(bobsledder) "James Morgan (bobsledder)") was killed in a crash during the four-man sled competition, resulted in the shortening of the track for future FIBT events.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBarnesHearn2001138-9)

The pre-credits sequence used the churchyard of the [Church of St Giles, Stoke Poges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Church_of_St_Giles,_Stoke_Poges "Church of St Giles, Stoke Poges"), [Buckinghamshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buckinghamshire "Buckinghamshire") as a cemetery, while the helicopter scenes were filmed at the abandoned [Beckton Gas Works](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beckton_Gas_Works "Beckton Gas Works") in London.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-locations-60) The gas works were also the location for some of [Stanley Kubrick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Kubrick "Stanley Kubrick")'s film, _[Full Metal Jacket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Full\_Metal\_Jacket "Full Metal Jacket")_ (1987).[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFalsetto2001xxii-65) Director John Glen gained the idea for the remote-controlled helicopter after seeing a child playing with an [RC car](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RC_car "RC car").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-inside-20) Since flying a helicopter through a warehouse was thought to be too dangerous, the scene was shot using [forced perspective](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forced_perspective "Forced perspective"). A smaller mock-up was built by [Derek Meddings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derek_Meddings "Derek Meddings")' team closer to the camera that the stunt pilot [Marc Wolff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marc_Wolff "Marc Wolff") flew behind and this made it seem as if the helicopter was entering the warehouse. The footage inside the building was shot on location, though with a life-sized helicopter model which stood over a rail. Stuntman [Martin Grace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Grace "Martin Grace") was a stand-in as Bond when the agent is dangling outside the flying helicopter, while Roger Moore himself was used in the scenes inside the model.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-glen-52)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-66) The helicopter _G-BAKS_, an [Agusta-Bell 206B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bell_206 "Bell 206") JetRanger II, crashed in fog on 14 November 1997, killing the pilot at [Cocking, West Sussex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cocking,_West_Sussex "Cocking, West Sussex"); it was built on 28 December 1972 for [Galliford Construction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galliford_Try "Galliford Try").[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-67)

### Music

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Music")]

Main article: [For Your Eyes Only (soundtrack)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(soundtrack) "For Your Eyes Only (soundtrack)")

The score of _For Your Eyes Only_ was written by [Bill Conti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Conti "Bill Conti"), who retained some [John Barry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Barry_(composer) "John Barry (composer)")-influenced brass elements in the score, but also added elements of dance and funk music.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-allmusic-68) While one reviewer observed that "Bill Conti's score is a constant source of annoyance",[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-Lee_Davies_(2008)-69) another claimed that "In the end, _For Your Eyes Only_ stands as one of the best James Bond film scores of the 1980s."[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-allmusic-68)

The [title song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(song) "For Your Eyes Only (song)"), written by Conti and Michael Leeson, was sung by [Sheena Easton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheena_Easton "Sheena Easton"), who was the only title song artist to perform it on screen in a Bond film,[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBenson1988231-30) as designer [Maurice Binder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maurice_Binder "Maurice Binder") liked Easton's appearance and decided to add her to the opening credits.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-70) The producers of the film hired [Debbie Harry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Debbie_Harry "Debbie Harry") to sing Conti and Leeson's song, but she quit when the producers refused to allow her band [Blondie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blondie_(band) "Blondie (band)") to write and perform an original song for the film.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-71) Blondie's rejected song, titled "For Your Eyes Only," can be found on their 1982 album, _[The Hunter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hunter\_(Blondie\_album) "The Hunter (Blondie album)")_.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-72)

## Release and reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Release and reception")]

_For Your Eyes Only_ was premiered at the [Odeon Leicester Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Odeon_Leicester_Square "Odeon Leicester Square") in London on 24 June 1981,[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-73) setting an all-time opening-day record for any film at any cinema in the UK with a gross of £14,998[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-PR_Newswire-74) (£57,819 in 2025 pounds[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-inflation-UK-75)).[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-PR_Newswire-74) The film entered general release in the UK the same day. It went on to gross £10.4 million in the UK.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-76)

_For Your Eyes Only_ had its North American premiere in Canada and the US on Friday 26 June, at approximately 1,100 cinemas.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-PR_Newswire-74)

The film grossed $54.8 million in the US and Canada[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-Numbers-Bond-77) (equivalent to $101.5 million at 2011 ticket prices[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-78) or $194 million in 2025 dollars,[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-inflation-US-79) adjusted for general inflation), and $195.3 million worldwide,[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBarnesHearn2001143-80) becoming the second highest grossing Bond film after its predecessor, _Moonraker_.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-Numbers-Bond-77) This was the last James Bond film to be solely released by [United Artists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Artists "United Artists"), as by this time its owner, [Transamerica Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transamerica_Corporation "Transamerica Corporation"), finalised the sale of the company to MGM. Following the MGM and United Artists merger, later runs including future entries were released under "MGM/UA Distribution Co".

The promotional cinema poster for the film featured a woman holding a [crossbow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crossbow "Crossbow"); she was photographed from behind, and her outfit left the bottom half of her buttocks exposed. The effect was achieved by having the model wear a pair of bikini bottoms backwards, so that the part seen on her backside is the front of the suit.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPfeifferWorrall1998131-81) The poster caused some furor—largely in the US—with _[The Boston Globe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Boston\_Globe "The Boston Globe")_ and the _[Los Angeles Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los\_Angeles\_Times "Los Angeles Times")_ considering the poster so unsuitable they edited out everything above the knee,[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-Time_(People)-82) whilst _[The Pittsburgh Press](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Pittsburgh\_Press "The Pittsburgh Press")_ editors painted a pair of shorts over the legs.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBarnesHearn2001140-83) There was significant speculation as to the identity of the model before photographer Morgan Kane identified her as Joyce Bartle.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-Time_(People)-82)

A number of items of merchandising were issued to coincide with the film, including a 007 digital watch and a copy of Melina's [Citroën 2CV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citro%C3%ABn_2CV "Citroën 2CV") by [Corgi Toys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corgi_Toys "Corgi Toys").[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPfeifferWorrall1998131-81)[Citroën](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citro%C3%ABn "Citroën") itself produced a special "007" edition of the 2CV, which even had decorative bullet holes on the door.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-84)[Marvel Comics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvel_Comics "Marvel Comics") also did a [comic book](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comic_book "Comic book") adaptation (see [section](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#Adaptations) below).[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPfeifferWorrall1998131-81)

### Television

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Television")]

_For Your Eyes Only_ had its US television premiere during [The ABC Sunday Night Movie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_ABC_Sunday_Night_Movie "The ABC Sunday Night Movie") on November 13, 1983.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-85) It delivered a 16.3 household rating, a 26% audience share, and nearly 25 million viewers in [Nielsen Media Research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nielsen_Media_Research "Nielsen Media Research") results, and finished as the 37th ranked program of the week. It was the first James Bond movie premiere on ABC to finish in third place in its time period instead of in second or first place since the two night premiere of _[On Her Majesty's Secret Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/On\_Her\_Majesty's\_Secret\_Service\_(film) "On Her Majesty's Secret Service (film)")_ in February 1976; however, it also ran against stiff competition including the network premiere of _[Airplane!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airplane! "Airplane!")_ on [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC") (18.9 rating, 29 share) and the first part of the highly rated [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS")[miniseries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miniseries "Miniseries")_[Chiefs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chiefs\_(miniseries) "Chiefs (miniseries)")_ (25.1 rating, 36 share).[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-86) A _For Your Eyes Only_ repeat on January 27, 1985, had stronger results, with a 19.4 rating and 28 share.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-87)

### Contemporary reviews

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Contemporary reviews")]

[Derek Malcolm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derek_Malcolm "Derek Malcolm") in _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Guardian "The Guardian")_ disliked the film, saying it was "too long... and pretty boring between the stunts", although he admitted that the stunts were of a high quality.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-Malcolm_(1981)-88) According to Malcolm, Bond "inhabits a fantasy-land of more or less bloodless violence, groinless sex and naivety masked as superior sophistication", with Moore playing him as if in a "nicely lubricated daze".[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-Malcolm_(1981)-88) Although Malcolm tipped the film for international box office success, he observed that he "can't quite see why the series has lasted so long and so strong in people's affections."[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-Malcolm_(1981)-88) Writing in _[The Observer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Observer "The Observer")_, [Philip French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philip_French "Philip French") commented that "not for the first time the pre-credits sequence is the best thing about the film."[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-French_(1981)-89) French was dismissive of Moore's Bond, saying that Bond was "impersonated by Moore" and referred to Moore's advancing years.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-French_(1981)-89)

[David Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Robinson_(film_critic) "David Robinson (film critic)"), writing in _[The Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Times "The Times")_ bemoaned the fact that the "dramatic bits between the set pieces don't count for much." Like other critics at the time his praise was more directed towards the stunt crews; they were "better than ever in this one."[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-90) The film critic for the magazine _[Time Out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time\_Out\_Group "Time Out Group")_ was brief and pithy: "no plot and poor dialogue, and Moore really is old enough to be the uncle of those girls."[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-91)

For the US press, Gary Arnold in _[The Washington Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Washington\_Post "The Washington Post")_ thought the film was "undeniably easy on the eyes", and further added "maybe too easy to prevent the mind from wandering and the lids from drooping."[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-Arnold_(1981)-92) Arnold was also critical of the large set pieces, calling them "more ponderous than sensational" and that there was "no equivalent of the classic action highlights that can be recalled readily from _From Russia with Love_ or _You Only Live Twice_ or _The Spy Who Loved Me_ or _Moonraker_. This is a Bond waiting for something inspired to push it over the top."[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-Arnold_(1981)-92)_[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_ critic [Vincent Canby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vincent_Canby "Vincent Canby") said that "_For Your Eyes Only_ is not the best of the series by a long shot" although he did say that the film is "slick entertainment" with a tone that is "consistently comic even when the material is not."[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-93)

[Jack Kroll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Kroll "Jack Kroll") in _[Newsweek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newsweek "Newsweek")_ dismissed the film, saying it was "an anthology of action episodes held together by the thinnest of plot lines", although he did concede that these set pieces are "terrific in their exhilaratingly absurd energy."[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-94) For _[Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time\_(magazine) "Time (magazine)")_ magazine, [Richard Corliss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Corliss "Richard Corliss") concentrated on the stunts, saying the team "have devised some splendid optional features for _For Your Eyes Only_" whilst also commenting on Roger Moore, saying that his "mannequin good looks and waxed-fruit insouciance" show him to be "the best-oiled cog in this perpetual motion machine."[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-95)[Jay Scott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Scott "Jay Scott") of _[The Globe and Mail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Globe\_and\_Mail "The Globe and Mail")_ included it on his list of the year's worst films,[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-Scott_(1981)-96) calling it "repellant"[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-Scott_(1983)-97) and "ambitiously bad".[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-Scott_(1981)-96)

French filmmaker [Robert Bresson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Bresson "Robert Bresson") admired the film: "It filled me with wonder because of its cinematographic writing... if I could have seen it twice in a row and again the next day, I would have done."[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-98)[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-99) Elsewhere Bresson said he also loved the film's ski chase.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-FOOTNOTECiment200936-100)

### Retrospective reviews

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Retrospective reviews")]

Opinion on _For Your Eyes Only_ has improved over time, with a 69% 'fresh' rating from [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"),[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-101) being ranked eleventh among the 24 Bond films.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-102) Ian Nathan of _[Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empire\_(magazine) "Empire (magazine)")_ gives the film only two of a possible five stars, observing that the film "still ranks as one of the most forgettable Bonds on record."[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-103) In 2006, [IGN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IGN "IGN") chose _For Your Eyes Only_ as the sixth-best Bond film, claiming it is "a good old-fashioned espionage tale",[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-104) a placement shared by Norman Wilner of [MSN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MSN "MSN"), who considered it "the one Moore film that seems to reach back to Connery's heyday",[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-105) and _[Entertainment Weekly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entertainment\_Weekly "Entertainment Weekly")_ chose it as the tenth best in 2008, saying it was a "return to low-tech, low-key Bond [with]... some of the best stunts since the early days".[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-106) In October 2008 _[Time Out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time\_Out\_Group "Time Out Group")_ re-issued a review of _For Your Eyes Only_ and observed that the film is "admirable in intent" but that it "feels a little spare", largely because the plot has been "divested of the bells and whistles that hallmark the franchise".[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-Lee_Davies_(2008)-69)

[James Berardinelli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Berardinelli "James Berardinelli") wrote that the film was "a solid adventure, although it could have been better",[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-107) while [Danny Peary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danny_Peary "Danny Peary") thought "There are exciting moments, but most of it is standard Bond fare," going on to describe _For Your Eyes Only_ as "an attempt to mix spectacle with [the] tough, believable storylines of early Bond films... [it] is enjoyable while you're watching it. Afterward, it's one of the most forgettable of the Bond series."[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPeary1986157-108)[Raymond Benson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raymond_Benson "Raymond Benson"), the author of nine Bond novels, thought _For Your Eyes Only_ was Roger Moore's best Bond film.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-109)

Although Chris Nashawaty of _Entertainment Weekly_ ranks Carole Bouquet playing Melina as the "worst babe" of the seven Roger Moore James Bond films,[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-110) his colleague, Joshua Rich disagreed, putting her tenth in the overall 10 Best Bond Girls listing from the 21 films released up to that point.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-111)_Entertainment Weekly_ also ranked Lynn-Holly Johnson as Bibi Dahl as ninth on their list of the 10 worst [Bond girls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bond_girl "Bond girl") from the 21 films that had been released.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-112) After 20 films had been released, IGN ranked Bouquet as fifth in their 'top 10 Bond Babes' list,[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-113) and _[The Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Times "The Times")_ thought she was sixth on their list of the Top 10 most fashionable Bond girls after 21 films had been released.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-114)

## Adaptations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Adaptations")]

Main article: [James Bond comic books](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Bond_comic_books "James Bond comic books")

[![Image 11: Two comic books covers, both titled "FOR YOUR EYES ONLY". The cover on the left shows a man with a pistol, with a blonde woman in front of him. In front of both of them a brunette woman holds a crossbow. The cover on the right shows the same man and brunette woman abseiling on a cliff, with two guns in the foreground pointing at them.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/0/04/FYEOcomicbook.jpg/250px-FYEOcomicbook.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:FYEOcomicbook.jpg)

Two-part _For Your Eyes Only_ comic book adaptation by Marvel Comics

As part of the merchandising of _For Your Eyes Only_, [Marvel Comics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvel_Comics "Marvel Comics") published an adaptation of the movie as issue 19 of _[Marvel Comics Super Special](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvel\_Comics\_Super\_Special "Marvel Comics Super Special")_; this was also repackaged as a two-issue comic book adaptation of the film.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPfeifferWorrall1998131-81)[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEThompsonFrankenhoffBickford2010368-121) The first issue was released in October 1981 and was soon followed by the second issue in November of the same year. The adaptation was written by [Larry Hama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_Hama "Larry Hama"), [pencilled](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penciller "Penciller") by [Howard Chaykin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Howard_Chaykin "Howard Chaykin"), [inked](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inker "Inker") by [Vincent Colletta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vincent_Colletta "Vincent Colletta"), and edited by [Dennis O'Neil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dennis_O'Neil "Dennis O'Neil").[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_Your_Eyes_Only_(film)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChaykin2011xvii-122)

It was the second film in the series to have a comic book tie-in, following a [_Dr. No_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr._No_(comics) "Dr. No (comics)") comic in 1962. Marvel Comics would go on to publish an _[Octopussy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Octopussy "Octopussy")_ comic book adaptation in 1983.

# Suffocating Heat

*   1991
*   1 Hr 41 Mins
*   Drama

On June 30, 1990, in Rome, Marie Christine is getting ready to take her son Pietro and Paolo to their father for the weekend. As the Football World Cup is taking place in Italy, Rome is flooded with supporters; the traffic is chaotic and French-born Marie Christine, who works as a translator, finds a bag that belongs to Miriam, who must leave the next day. Marie Christine decides to find her to return her passport, but one Giuliano Ferrini tries to prevent this. So Marie Christine finds herself navigating through a hot Roman night in a city she doesn't know, among people she never dreamed could inhabit the same city.

### Inhalt

Dieb Lello (Ben Gazzara) braucht für die Silvesternacht einen Partner an den er das Diebesgut weiterreichen kann, denn es ist Lellos Prinzip, niemals Diebesware am Körper zu behalten. Man schlägt ihm den Kleingauner Umberto „Infortunio“ (Unfall) Pennazzuto (Totò) vor, und die beiden verabreden sich.

Umberto hatte zunächst andere Pläne. Wie im Jahr zuvor will er sich mit seiner alten Bekannten Gioia „Tortorella“ (Turteltaube) Fabbricotti verabreden, doch Gioia wurde bereits zu einer anderen Party eingeladen, allerdings nur, weil man nicht mit einer Unglückszahl von 13 Gästen feiern wollte. ### Inhalt

Dieb Lello (Ben Gazzara) braucht für die Silvesternacht einen Partner an den er das Diebesgut weiterreichen kann, denn es ist Lellos Prinzip, niemals Diebesware am Körper zu behalten. Man schlägt ihm den Kleingauner Umberto „Infortunio“ (Unfall) Pennazzuto (Totò) vor, und die beiden verabreden sich.

Umberto hatte zunächst andere Pläne. Wie im Jahr zuvor will er sich mit seiner alten Bekannten Gioia „Tortorella“ (Turteltaube) Fabbricotti verabreden, doch Gioia wurde bereits zu einer anderen Party eingeladen, allerdings nur, weil man nicht mit einer Unglückszahl von 13 Gästen feiern wollte. ### Inhalt

Der Jurastudent Roberto Mariani (Jean-Louis Trintignant) bereitet sich gerade auf seinen Abschluss vor, während er gelegentlich schmachtend Valeria von gegenüber beobachtet, für die er zwar eine Schwäche, aber nie gewagt hat, tatsächlich mit ihr zu sprechen. Unterbrochen wird er von dem ihm völlig unbekannten Bruno Cortona (Vittorio Gassman), der ihn am Fenster stehen sieht und ihn darum bittet, ob er eine Freundin von ihm anrufen könne, um ihr zu sagen, dass er – Bruno - sich verspätet. Roberto bittet ihn herein und findet sich kurz darauf in Brunos Cabrio wieder, der ihn auf eine Spritztour in seinem Cabrio mitnimmt.

Die beiden Männer könnten kaum verschiedener sein. Roberto, zögerlich, bieder, auf seine Zukunft bedacht. Sieht er ein Mädchen, das ihm gefällt, sagt ihm seine Erziehung dass er sie dann auch heiraten muss. Bruno dagegen ist ein extrovertierter, leichtlebiger Windhund, Mitte Dreißig und in windigen Geschäften tätig, wie es scheint.

Und so führt die Fahrt der Beiden die so unterschiedlichen Männer aufs Land, bis ihre Fahrt sie nach zwei Tagen und einer Prügelei zu Brunos Familie im Ferienort Viareggio führt.

### Inhalt

Der Jurastudent Roberto Mariani (Jean-Louis Trintignant) bereitet sich gerade auf seinen Abschluss vor, während er gelegentlich schmachtend Valeria von gegenüber beobachtet, für die er zwar eine Schwäche, aber nie gewagt hat, tatsächlich mit ihr zu sprechen. Unterbrochen wird er von dem ihm völlig unbekannten Bruno Cortona (Vittorio Gassman), der ihn am Fenster stehen sieht und ihn darum bittet, ob er eine Freundin von ihm anrufen könne, um ihr zu sagen, dass er – Bruno - sich verspätet. Roberto bittet ihn herein und findet sich kurz darauf in Brunos Cabrio wieder, der ihn auf eine Spritztour in seinem Cabrio mitnimmt.

Die beiden Männer könnten kaum verschiedener sein. Roberto, zögerlich, bieder, auf seine Zukunft bedacht. Sieht er ein Mädchen, das ihm gefällt, sagt ihm seine Erziehung dass er sie dann auch heiraten muss. Bruno dagegen ist ein extrovertierter, leichtlebiger Windhund, Mitte Dreißig und in windigen Geschäften tätig, wie es scheint.

Und so führt die Fahrt der Beiden die so unterschiedlichen Männer aufs Land, bis ihre Fahrt sie nach zwei Tagen und einer Prügelei zu Brunos Familie im Ferienort Viareggio führt.

# These Are the Best Shows to Watch Based on Shows You Already Love

Our recommendations for shows like Interview with the Vampire, The Bear, Severance, and more

![Image 2: Kelly Connolly](https://www.tvguide.com/a/img/resize/bc7a760e430ebb2c1e826eb097cbf0a7a882285e/hub/2022/07/13/0f3e0fa9-e74a-4957-a71d-a9548ea88bd9/kc-profile-pic.jpg?auto=webp&height=88&quality=70&width=88)

![Image 3: Kaitlin Thomas](https://www.tvguide.com/a/img/resize/f186318391f0ec6877914fffe445a308226c7e2a/hub/2017/10/20/65d69ccc-06f7-486e-98a3-c4475fac26d4/kaitlin-photo1.jpg?auto=webp&height=88&quality=70&width=88)

[Kelly Connolly](https://www.tvguide.com/authors/kelly.connolly/),[Kaitlin Thomas](https://www.tvguide.com/authors/kaitlin.thomas/)

Aug. 9, 2023

Starting a new TV show has a way of setting off a chain reaction: You watch a show, you like it, you look for something else that actor is in, and you find yourself watching _Yellowstone_. And then you have to watch _1883_! One show tends to lead to the next. If you're looking for new favorite shows that will remind you of your old favorite shows, you've come to the right place. TV Guide has put together countless lists of the best shows to watch based on the shows you already love. Some of our recommendations are similar in tone; some share the same creator or stars; and some will get you thinking about the same big ideas.

Below, you will find an alphabetized list of all of our current lists of recommendations based on shows you like. If you don't see a show you like, check back soon, as we're updating our catalog regularly. And if there's a show you're interested in and would like us to cover and recommend similar shows for, please [let us know](https://twitter.com/TVGuide)!

* * *

### [Shows to Watch If You Like _The 100_](https://www.tvguide.com/news/shows-like-the-100-to-watch-while-you-wait-for-season-7-to-hit-netflix/)

If you're still processing The CW's epic sci-fi series about teens starting society over, we've got more dystopian, apocalyptic, teen-centric series to watch.

### [Shows to Watch If You Like _1883_](https://www.tvguide.com/news/7-shows-like-1883-to-watch-if-you-like-1883/)

If you love _Yellowstone_, then you probably also love its prequel spinoff, _[1883](https://www.tvguide.com/tvshows/1883/1060062715/)_, starring[Tim McGraw](https://www.tvguide.com/celebrities/tim-mcgraw/3000396075/), [Faith Hill](https://www.tvguide.com/celebrities/faith-hill/3030386518/), and [Isabel May](https://www.tvguide.com/celebrities/isabel-may/3000859255/)as the Duttons of a bygone era. And if you want more, [we have a list of shows like _Yellowstone_](https://www.tvguide.com/news/shows-like-yellowstone-what-to-watch-next/), too.

### [Shows to Watch If You Like _Abbott Elementary_](https://www.tvguide.com/news/shows-like-abbott-elementary-abc-season-2-watch-next/)

Created by and starring[Quinta Brunson](https://www.tvguide.com/celebrities/quinta-brunson/3030862494/), this [delightful ABC workplace comedy](https://www.tvguide.com/news/features/abbott-elementary-best-show-on-tv/) about the staff at a Philadelphia elementary school has been a welcome addition to our TV viewing schedules. If you're on the lookout for shows with similar sensibilities, other shows about teachers, or simply more Quinta Brunson, we have a few recommendations that you can check out.

Advertisement

### [Shows to Watch If You Like _All American_](https://www.tvguide.com/news/shows-like-all-american-season-3-cw-netflix-what-to-watch-next/)

Go long and check out these shows guaranteed to score with fans of The CW's _[All American](https://www.tvguide.com/tvshows/all-american/1030289871/)_, whether you're into the teen drama, the social issues, or the epic highs and lows of high school football. There are even (gasp) shows about other sports.

### [Shows to Watch If You Like _Alone_](https://www.tvguide.com/news/shows-like-alone-history-channel-netflix-what-to-watch-next/)

History's reality competition[_Alone_](https://www.tvguide.com/tvshows/alone/797363/)drops rugged survivalists into remote wilderness all over the world and challenges them to stay alive. If this sounds like fun to you, here are some similar shows that range from harsh competitions featuring amateurs to educational survival shows hosted by trained professionals.

### [Shows to Watch If You Like _American Horror Story_](https://www.tvguide.com/news/9-shows-like-american-horror-story-recommendations-ahs-double-feature-season-10/)

_[American Horror Story](https://www.tvguide.com/tvshows/american-horror-story/1000385585/)_ has been so successful for creator Ryan Murphy and FX that both seem intent on making the show until they're in their graves. If you can't get enough, here are more series, from campy thrillers to deeply unsettling dramas, that should satisfy your thirst.

### [Shows to Watch If You Like _Animal Kingdom_](https://www.tvguide.com/news/7-shows-like-animal-kingdom-to-watch-if-you-like-animal-kingdom/)

If you're missing TNT's sun-kissed SoCal crime drama[_Animal Kingdom_](https://www.tvguide.com/tvshows/animal-kingdom/1000576866/), try these macho family dramas about brothers (or brothers in arms) who do crime together. We're confident you'll find something that floats your surfboard.

### [Shows to Watch If You Like _Atlanta_](https://www.tvguide.com/news/shows-like-atlanta-season-4-fx-watch-next/)

_[Atlanta](https://www.tvguide.com/tvshows/atlanta/1030514833/)_,[Donald Glover](https://www.tvguide.com/celebrities/donald-glover/credits/3030322526/)'s hypnotic FX comedy,is unlike anything else on TV — but here's a list of shows that come as close as we could get. Our recommendations for what to watch after _Atlanta_ include similarly surreal series, comedies about young people trying to make it in the world, and immersive shows with well-crafted worlds.

Advertisement

### [Shows to Watch If You Like _Avatar: The Last Airbender_](https://www.tvguide.com/news/shows-like-avatar-the-last-airbender-what-to-watch-next/)

_[Avatar: The Last Airbender](https://www.tvguide.com/tvshows/avatar-the-last-airbender/194673/)_ is an animated adventure series following Aang ([Zach Tyler Eisen](https://www.tvguide.com/celebrities/zach-tyler-eisen/282024/)), a 12-year-old boy who teams up with his friends to end an oppressive regime using his unique ability to "bend" all four elements: water, fire, earth, and air. After you finish the series, check out these other shows about super-powered teens, embarking on magical quests, and growing up in a weird, scary world.

### [Shows to Watch If You Like _Barry_](https://www.tvguide.com/news/shows-like-barry-hbo-season-3-watch-next/)

Luckily,[Bill Hader](https://www.tvguide.com/celebrities/bill-hader/3000054340/)'s tortured hitman/wannabe actor Barry Berkman/Block is nowhere near the first TV murderer to have feelings. If you're in the market for more, our list of shows like _Barry_ includes dark comedies, killers for hire, and a whole lot of weirdos doing crime.

### [Shows to Watch If You Like _The Bear_](https://www.tvguide.com/news/shows-like-the-bear-season-2-hulu-fx/)

Ready for more shows like _[The Bear](https://www.tvguide.com/tvshows/the-bear/1000976418/)_? Yes, Chef! We've rounded up some recommendations for other family dramedies, series about chaotic workplaces, and shows about food. Consider this list your very own _The Bear_-inspired tasting menu.

![Image 4: Rhea Seehorn and Bob Odenkirk, Better Call Saul](https://www.tvguide.com/a/img/resize/a1bd7df73c6a8595fd0da22000936dbe33ba4bd9/hub/2021/02/16/1c0d0b7e-ff63-4bca-8bf7-6cd16e16a841/better-call-saul-kim-jimmy-court.jpg?auto=webp&quality=70&width=1096)

Rhea Seehorn and Bob Odenkirk,_Better Call Saul_

Greg Lewis/AMC/Sony Pictures Television

### [Shows to Watch If You Like _Better Call Saul_](https://www.tvguide.com/news/shows-like-better-call-saul-season-6-part-2/)

Saul may be gone, but all hope is not lost. In honor of [one of the greatest TV dramas](https://www.tvguide.com/news/features/better-call-saul-best-show-on-tv/) of our time, we've put together a list of shows that share similarities with _Better Call Saul_, whether they present a different look at being a lawyer, involve slick cons and slicker conmen, or are darkly comedic with serious stakes.

### [Shows to Watch If You Like _The Big Bang Theory_](https://www.tvguide.com/news/shows-like-the-big-bang-theory-what-to-watch-next/)

[_The Big Bang Theory_](https://www.tvguide.com/tvshows/the-big-bang-theory/288041/), the CBS sitcom about a group of nerdy friends who know everything about science and geek culture but are clueless about love, was the biggest comedy on TV for many years. This list has comedies and light dramas with a will they/won't they relationship, a charismatic oddball breakout character, an appreciation for the scientific, or all of the above.

Advertisement

### [Shows to Watch If You Like _Billions_](https://www.tvguide.com/news/shows-like-billions-you-should-watch-if-you-like-billions/)

Cash in on our wealth of knowledge with this list of great,_[Billions](https://www.tvguide.com/tvshows/billions/713140/)_-esque shows. Whether they've got a one percent of the one percent New York City setting, twisty legal and financial dealmaking and double-crossing, or flavorful dialogue, these shows are all a little bit _Billions_.

### [Shows to Watch If You Like _Black Mirror_](https://www.tvguide.com/news/shows-like-black-mirror-netflix-hulu-amazon/)

If you've already downloaded all of _[Black Mirror](https://www.tvguide.com/tvshows/black-mirror/520746/)_ into your brain, check out these shows: most are sci-fi, some are anthologies, and some are from _Black Mirror_ creator Charlie Brooker, but all of them will leave you saying, "Whaaaaaaaaaaaaaat?"

### [Shows to Watch If You Like _The Blacklist_](https://www.tvguide.com/news/shows-like-the-blacklist-season-8-what-to-watch-next/)

The shows on this list include action shows with a combination of serialized and episodic storytelling, a dynamic like the one between Red ([James Spader](https://www.tvguide.com/celebrities/james-spader/155526/)) and FBI Agent Liz Keen ([Megan Boone](https://www.tvguide.com/celebrities/megan-boone/304079/)), a task force with funny sidekicks, and _The Blacklist_'s most important ingredient, James Spader himself. This list reminds us of the time we were eating breakfast octopus on the Adriatic coast with the most beautiful Romanian textile heiress...

### [Shows to Watch If You Like _Blindspot_](https://www.tvguide.com/news/shows-like-blindspot-what-to-watch-next-action-shows/)

NBC's action thriller[_Blindspot_](https://www.tvguide.com/tvshows/blindspot/800996/)starred[Jaimie Alexander](https://www.tvguide.com/celebrities/jaimie-alexander/241662/)as a tattooed amnesiac sleeper agent and[Sullivan Stapleton](https://www.tvguide.com/celebrities/sullivan-stapleton/328778/)as her FBI handler-turned-husband. Our list of recommendations includes shows that feature some combination of action, amnesia, conspiracy, an ass-kicking heroine, an unlikely partnership between a weird loner and a federal agency, and a casual sense of humor.

### [Shows to Watch If You Like _Blue Bloods_](https://www.tvguide.com/news/8-shows-like-blue-bloods-to-watch-if-you-like-blue-bloods/)

If[Tom Selleck](https://www.tvguide.com/celebrities/tom-selleck/3000200733/)'s Frank Reagan is your kind of TV character, what else should you watch? We've compiled a list of shows that share similar DNA with _[Blue Bloods](https://www.tvguide.com/tvshows/blue-bloods/1000297396/)_, whether they're great cop shows or series about families in business together.

Advertisement

### [Shows to Watch If You Like _The Bold Type_](https://www.tvguide.com/news/shows-like-the-bold-type-hulu-netflix/)

Even though we've said goodbye to Jane ([Katie Stevens](https://www.tvguide.com/celebrities/katie-stevens/302636/#link=%257B%2522role%2522:%2522standard%2522,%2522href%2522:%2522https:/www.tvguide.com/celebrities/katie-stevens/302636/%2522,%2522target%2522:%2522_blank%2522,%2522absolute%2522:%2522%2522,%2522linkText%2522:%2522Katie%2520Stevens%2522%257D)), Kat ([Aisha Dee](https://www.tvguide.com/celebrities/aisha-dee/319714/#link=%257B%2522role%2522:%2522standard%2522,%2522href%2522:%2522https:/www.tvguide.com/celebrities/aisha-dee/319714/%2522,%2522target%2522:%2522_blank%2522,%2522absolute%2522:%2522%2522,%2522linkText%2522:%2522Aisha%2520Dee%2522%257D)), Sutton ([Meghann Fahy](https://www.tvguide.com/celebrities/meghann-fahy/304253/#link=%257B%2522role%2522:%2522standard%2522,%2522href%2522:%2522https:/www.tvguide.com/celebrities/meghann-fahy/304253/%2522,%2522target%2522:%2522_blank%2522,%2522absolute%2522:%2522%2522,%2522linkText%2522:%2522Meghann%2520Fahy%2522%257D)), and their cohort at _Scarlet_, there are plenty of fun shows out there that will help fill the void. Think of this list as your own personal piece of highly specific, conveniently timed life advice from Jacqueline ([Melora Hardin](https://www.tvguide.com/celebrities/melora-hardin/3000414043/)).

### [Shows to Watch If You Like _Bones_](https://www.tvguide.com/news/9-shows-like-bones-for-you-to-watch-if-you-like-bones/)

There are more episodes of[_Bones_](https://www.tvguide.com/tvshows/bones/1000399820/)than there are bones in the human body, so it's easy to pass a lot of time watching _Bones_. But if you're looking for the next show to fill that Jeffersonian-sized hole in your life, there's a little something for everyone on this list, whether you kept coming back to _Bones_ for the electric romance between Booth and Brennan, the cool science, the freaky science, or the banter between smart hot people.

### [Shows to Watch If You Like _Bosch_](https://www.tvguide.com/news/shows-like-bosch-season-6-what-to-watch-next/)

[_Bosch_](https://www.tvguide.com/tvshows/bosch/635724/), Amazon's adaptation of Michael Connelly's Harry Bosch novels, is an authentic crime drama detailing the life of L.A. homicide detective and private investigator Harry Bosch ([Titus Welliver](https://www.tvguide.com/celebrities/titus-welliver/176999/)). Our list of recommendations features other great police dramas, some murder mysteries, and shows with complicated men at their center.

### [Shows to Watch If You Like _The Boys_](https://www.tvguide.com/news/shows-like-the-boys-season-3-what-to-watch-next-amazon-netflix-hulu/)

There can never be enough of [_The Boys_](https://www.tvguide.com/tvshows/the-boys/1135867/). Thankfully, there are other shows out there that will fulfill your desire for depraved humor, ridiculous violence, and[Antony Starr](https://www.tvguide.com/celebrities/antony-starr/288811/)'s jaw. In our list of recommendations, you'll find new takes on superhero shows, dark adaptations of comic books, and series featuring _The Boys_ cast members, and they're all pre-approved to be good.

### [Shows to Watch If You Like _Breaking Bad_](https://www.tvguide.com/news/10-shows-like-breaking-bad-watch-next/)

Since _[Breaking Bad](https://www.tvguide.com/tvshows/breaking-bad/1030019630/)_ aired its series finale, we've seen numerous shows inspired by[Vince Gilligan](https://www.tvguide.com/celebrities/vince-gilligan/3000426723/)'s masterpiece, as well as a spin-off that somehow managed to not only live up to but exceed the expectations set by the original show. We all miss _Breaking Bad_, and there's really nothing quite like it, but we've gathered a handful of shows that could potentially fill the Walter White-sized hole in your TV watchlist.

Advertisement

![Image 5: Simone Ashley and Jonathan Bailey, Bridgerton](https://www.tvguide.com/a/img/resize/5ef032043c406a6ff7a4913c4c5fe5c416c62a5d/hub/2022/05/17/04453a52-d45e-4908-9586-cda6a6c732e7/bridgerton-205-unit-02118r.jpg?auto=webp&quality=70&width=1096)

Simone Ashley and Jonathan Bailey, _Bridgerton_

### [Shows to Watch If You Like _Bridgerton_](https://www.tvguide.com/news/shows-like-bridgerton-shonda-rhimes-netflix-what-to-watch-next/)

_[Bridgerton](https://www.tvguide.com/tvshows/bridgerton/1337399/)_ is a reminder that period pieces don't have to be stuffy melodrama for your grandmama. They can be titillating tales of sins and secrets among attractive aristocrats. Here's a list of more shows that scratch the same itch, whether you're looking for lustful hookups, copious amounts of scandal and gossip, or historical dramas with a surprisingly modern tone.

### [Shows to Watch If You Like _Buffy the Vampire Slayer_](https://www.tvguide.com/news/10-shows-like-buffy-the-vampire-slayer-watch-next-hulu/)

Over the course of[_Buffy the Vampire Slayer_](https://www.tvguide.com/tvshows/buffy-the-vampire-slayer/1000293659/)'s seven seasons, Buffy Summers ([Sarah Michelle Gellar](https://www.tvguide.com/celebrities/sarah-michelle-gellar/3030418122/)) changed TV for good. So many of today's tough action heroines, witty teens, and supernatural love triangles all owe something to _Buffy_. If you're missing the Scooby Gang but looking to check out something new, you'll find pieces of _Buffy_ in all of the shows on this list.

### [Shows to Watch If You Like _Chesapeake Shores_](https://www.tvguide.com/news/7-shows-like-chesapeake-shores-hallmark-netflix-hulu/)

If you're like us, there's a void in your life when Hallmark's heartfelt family drama _Chesapeake Shores_ isn't airing. It's a good thing this list of similar romantic series and family dramas just washed up on shore.

### [Shows to Watch If You Like _Cobra Kai_](https://www.tvguide.com/news/shows-like-cobra-kai-what-to-watch-next-netflix-season-3/)

Picking up 34 years after the events of _[The Karate Kid](https://www.tvguide.com/movies/the-karate-kid/103043/)_ films,_[Cobra Kai](https://www.tvguide.com/tvshows/cobra-kai/1098619/)_ reunites its stars[Ralph Macchio](https://www.tvguide.com/celebrities/ralph-macchio/170787/)and[William Zabka](https://www.tvguide.com/celebrities/william-zabka/179319/)in their roles as Daniel and Johnny to examine what happens when their rivalry reignites vis-à-vis their teenage children, who are also — you guessed it — into karate. Here are more shows that tap into nostalgia, feel-goodness, and punching.
